_meta.page_convention: Page numbers refer to printed book pages (as shown in the page footers), not PDF indices.
_meta.notes: Tooltip-friendly. Short, concrete, player-readable. Skill base = linked aptitude x 1, except Fray (REF x 2) and Perceive (INT x 2).

COG.name: Cognition
COG.short: Your intelligence, problem-solving, and capacity for logical analysis.
COG.used_for: Memory, study, and technical thought. Roll COG x 3 to recall a fact, memorize a number, or resist mental manipulation. Adds its value to linked skills.

INT.name: Intuition
INT.short: Your gut instinct, awareness, creativity, and cleverness.
INT.used_for: Sizing things up on the fly. Roll INT x 3 to read a situation, see through an illusion, or grok alien intent. Adds its value to linked skills (and to Perceive doubled).

REF.name: Reflexes
REF.short: Your coordination, dexterity, balance, and reaction speed.
REF.used_for: Snap reactions and fine motor work. Roll REF x 3 to catch a thrown object, balance, or avoid blinding glare. Adds its value to linked skills (and to Fray doubled).

SAV.name: Savvy
SAV.short: Your social awareness, adaptability, empathy, and influence.
SAV.used_for: Reading rooms and people. Roll SAV x 3 to size up a social situation, follow etiquette, or resist social manipulation. Adds its value to linked skills.

SOM.name: Somatics
SOM.short: How well you exploit your morph's body: strength, stamina, sustained motion.
SOM.used_for: Raw physicality. Roll SOM x 3 for brute strength, to endure hardship, or to break a grapple. Adds its value to linked skills.

WIL.name: Willpower
WIL.short: Your self-control, mental fortitude, and strength of personality.
WIL.used_for: Resolve under pressure. Roll WIL x 3 to keep composure, resist fear, or shrug off emotional manipulation. Also drives Psi and resists Provoke. Determines Lucidity (mental HP).

aptitudeCheck.short: When no skill applies but raw talent does, roll d100 against Aptitude x 3.
aptitudeCheck.examples: Recall a memory (COG), see through an illusion (INT), catch a thrown object (REF), follow etiquette (SAV), break a grapple (SOM), resist fear (WIL).

Insight.short: Your mental pool. Boosts COG/INT and their linked skills.
Insight.used_for: Spend 1 point on a linked test for one of: ignore all modifiers, +20 to target, flip-flop your roll (e.g. 83 to 38), upgrade a success, or downgrade a critical failure. Also: take initiative for mental/mesh actions, take an extra mental/mesh action, or acquire a clue without rolling.

Moxie.short: Your social pool. Boosts SAV/WIL and their linked skills. Also fuels Rep Tests.
Moxie.used_for: Spend 1 point on a linked test for the usual options (ignore modifiers, +20, flip-flop, upgrade success, downgrade crit-fail). Also: ignore 1 trauma for 24h, refresh a Minor (1) or Moderate (2) rep favor, get a tip without rolling, negate a player gaffe, or skip an Infection Test on a sleight (asyncs).

Vigor.short: Your physical pool. Boosts REF/SOM and their linked skills.
Vigor.used_for: Spend 1 point on a linked test for the usual options (ignore modifiers, +20, flip-flop, upgrade success, downgrade crit-fail). Also: take initiative, take an extra physical action, or ignore 1 wound for 24h.

Flex.short: Your wild-card pool. Works on ANY test, plus narrative control.
Flex.used_for: Spend 1 on any test for the usual options. Or spend for narrative control: introduce a plausible NPC, item, environmental detail, or a minor relationship with an existing NPC.

_recharge.short_recharge: 10 min task action, twice per 24h. Restores 1d6 pool points you allocate.
_recharge.long_recharge: 4 hours (8 for flats), once per 24h. Fully restores all pools.
_recharge.max_bonus: Ware, drugs, and sleights can boost a pool by at most +5.

Initiative.name: Initiative
Initiative.used_for: Determines turn order in combat. Roll 1d6 + Initiative; highest goes first. Spend Vigor (any actions) or Insight (mental/mesh only) to go first this turn.

WT.name: Wound Threshold
WT.used_for: Any single hit that deals damage equal to or above WT inflicts a wound. Each wound is a cumulative -10 to actions and -1 Initiative, and forces a SOM Check to stay standing.

DUR.name: Durability
DUR.used_for: Your physical HP. Hit DUR in total damage and you're unconscious (biomorph) or crashed (synthmorph). Hit your Death Rating and the body dies.

DR.name: Death Rating
DR.formula: DUR x 1.5 (biomorph) or DUR x 2 (synthmorph / infomorph)
DR.used_for: Total damage that destroys this body. Biomorphs die; synthmorphs are wrecked beyond repair. Your ego survives if your cortical stack is recovered or you have a backup.

TT.name: Trauma Threshold
TT.used_for: Any single stress hit equal to or above TT inflicts a trauma. Each trauma is a cumulative -10 to actions and -1 Initiative, plus a WIL Check to avoid being stunned.

LUC.name: Lucidity
LUC.used_for: Your mental HP. Accumulate stress equal to LUC and your ego has a breakdown: 1d6 hours catatonic, plus a new Mental Disorder trait.

IR.name: Insanity Rating
IR.used_for: If accumulated stress ever reaches IR, your mind is permanently and irrecoverably lost. No psychosurgery, no rest, brings it back.

InfectionRating.name: Infection Rating (asyncs only)
InfectionRating.used_for: Strength of the Watts-MacLeod exovirus's hold on you. Rises when you use psi-gamma sleights or push a sleight; recharging lowers it. Higher IR means stronger compulsions and side effects.

Athletics.used_for: Physical action in gravity with a humanoid or biomimicked morph: climb, jump, swim, run, parkour, throw a grenade.

Deceive.used_for: Lying, bluffing, conning, fast talk, impersonation, acting. Opposed by the target's Kinesics.

Exotic Skill.note: Field skill - pick a specific subject (Disguise, Bow, Sleight of Hand, Animal Handling, etc.).
Exotic Skill.used_for: Catch-all for narrow trained skills not covered elsewhere. Each field is its own skill.

Fray.note: Special: base = REF x 2, not x 1.
Fray.used_for: Dodging. Opposes melee and ranged attacks; halved vs. guns. Also used to avoid falling objects, slip through a crowd, or sidestep collisions.

Free Fall.used_for: Microgravity and free-fall maneuvering: push down a micrograv tunnel, drift across zero g, vacsuit jets, parachute, recover from a spin.

Guns.used_for: Shooting beam, kinetic, seeker, and spray weapons. Attacks are opposed with the target's Fray / 2.

Hardware.note: Field skill - pick a field (Aerospace, Armorer, Demolitions, Electronics, Groundcraft, Industrial, Nautical, Robotics).
Hardware.used_for: Designing, building, repairing, and altering physical tech: fix a life support system, upgrade a robot, pick an electronic lock, place explosives.

Infiltrate.used_for: Sneaking, hiding, shadowing, blending into a crowd, concealing objects, evading sensors. Opposed by Perceive.

Infosec.used_for: Hacking and counter-hacking: break into systems, subvert and protect them, encrypt and decrypt files. Most uses are task actions.

Interface.used_for: Using and understanding electronics, software, sensors, and mesh devices: scan for wireless, jam frequencies, forge video, command life support. Also used to fire mounted/vehicle weapon systems.

Kinesics.used_for: Reading body language: detect lies, read emotional state, judge intent, use nonverbal cues. Opposes Deceive. -30 to read synthmorphs.

Know.note: Field skill - pick a topic (Engineering, Biology, Hypercorp Politics, Police Ops, Triads, etc.).
Know.used_for: What you know. Recall facts, analyze clues, identify weaknesses, plan, appraise, or supply a Complementary Skill bonus to an Active skill test (+10/+20/+30 at 40/60/80).

Medicine.note: Field skill - pick a field (Biotech, Forensics, Paramedic, Pharmacology, Psychosurgery, Veterinary).
Medicine.used_for: Healthcare, diagnosis, and biological design. Paramedic patches wounds; Biotech installs implants; Psychosurgery heals mental trauma; Pharmacology brews drugs and antidotes.

Melee.used_for: Hand-to-hand fighting: punch, kick, grapple, blade, club, implanted weapons. Opposed by Fray (dodge) or Melee (block/parry).

Perceive.note: Special: base = INT x 2, not x 1.
Perceive.used_for: Spotting things: notice intruders, find clues, locate traps, search rooms, scrounge. Basic perception is automatic (-20 distracted); detailed is a quick action; thorough is a task action. Opposes Infiltrate.

Persuade.used_for: Logical/reasoned social influence: bargain, negotiate, convince a reluctant party, motivate allies. Opposed by SAV Check. (Emotional pressure is Provoke.)

Pilot.note: Field skill - pick a field (Air, Ground, Nautical, Space).
Pilot.used_for: Maneuvering vehicles, bots, and non-humanoid morphs that don't move with limbs: drift a car, evade pursuit, barrel-roll a plane, run a high-g spacecraft burn.

Program.used_for: Writing and modifying code: scripts, malware, patches, AR/VR illusions, nanofab blueprints, infomorph mind-states.

Provoke.used_for: Emotional social manipulation: taunt, intimidate, browbeat, seduce, rile a mob. Opposed by WIL Check.

Psi.note: Requires the Psi trait. Default to WIL if untrained.
Psi.used_for: Targeting others with psi-gamma sleights. Opposed by the target's WIL Check.

Research.used_for: Finding things online: look up an answer on the mesh, track people, search archives, mine data dumps, navigate the deep mesh.

Survival.used_for: Wilderness and hostile-environment competence: navigate, track, forage, find safe shelter, handle ecological hazards.

rep.short: Your standing in 1 of 7 transhuman social networks. The score is your target number for Rep Tests.
rep.used_for: Call in favors (info, gear, contacts, lodging, intros). Roll d100 vs. your rep score. Higher score = bigger favors. Burning a favor temporarily reduces what you can request from that network until you refresh.

networks.@-rep: The Circle-A List. Autonomists, anarchists, Titanians, scum swarms, Extropians.
networks.c-rep: CivicNet. The Planetary Consortium, Morningstar, Lunar-Lagrange Alliance, Jovian Republic, hypercorps and capitalists.
networks.f-rep: Fame. The media network of metacelebrities, journalists, socialites, artists, and glitterati.
networks.g-rep: Guanxi. Triads, cartels, gangs, and other criminal networks.
networks.i-rep: The Eye. Firewall's secret internal reputation network.
networks.r-rep: Research Network Affiliates. Argonauts, scientists, technologists, and academic researchers.

motivations.short: Three personal goals (+ supports, - opposes) that drive your character.
motivations.used_for: Earn Rez Points for advancement by pursuing them, and cope with mental trauma: hitting a motivational goal heals 1d6 stress (or 1 trauma if no stress), and gives +20 to the next test to remove a disorder. Typically 1 from your faction plus 2 personal.

basic.short: Roll d100 (percentile). Equal to or under your target number = success. Over = failure.

criticals.short: Doubles (00, 11, 22 ...) = critical. Roll of 00 always critical success; 99 always critical failure.

superior_results.short: 33/66 rule: a successful roll of 33+ is a superior success; 66+ is two. A failed roll of 66 or less is a superior failure; 33 or less is two. Use them to gain extra detail, time, damage, quality, or covertness.

defaulting.short: Lacking a skill, you can roll against its linked aptitude (no x3 multiplier - just the aptitude value). No modifier, but critical successes are ignored.

teamwork.short: Helpers give the rolling character +10 each, up to +30. Only the roller can spend pools on the test.

opposed.short: Both sides roll. If one succeeds and one fails, success wins. If both succeed, higher roll wins. Critical successes beat non-criticals regardless of roll.

biomorph.name: Biomorph
biomorph.short: A fully biological body, often genefixed and fitted with implants. Birthed or vat-grown, then raised to adulthood.
biomorph.used_for: The default transhuman experience. Moderate DUR (25-45), no innate armor, full social acceptance everywhere, normal biological needs (food, sleep, air), heals naturally and via medichines/healing vat. Death Rating = DUR x 1.5.

synthmorph.name: Synthmorph
synthmorph.short: A robotic shell powered by batteries or nuclear cells. Built to last, with integral armor.
synthmorph.used_for: Tougher than biomorphs (built-in Armor and higher Death Rating = DUR x 2). No biological needs, immune to toxins/disease/most temperature and vacuum, ignores 1 wound (pain filter). Bears a 'Clanking Masses' social stigma in many habitats. Shock attacks scramble mesh actions; unarmed strikes do 2d6.

pod.name: Pod
pod.short: A vat-grown biological body driven by a cyberbrain rather than natural neurology. The fast-and-cheap alternative to a true biomorph.
pod.used_for: Looks and bleeds like a biomorph, but the brain is digital — vulnerable to hacking and to all cyberbrain attacks. Often visible seamlines mark them. Comes with Access Jacks, Cyberbrain, Mnemonics, and Puppet Sock. Carries a pod social stigma in many habitats. Death Rating = DUR x 1.5 like a biomorph.

infomorph.name: Infomorph
infomorph.short: A purely digital body — software you run on mesh servers and devices. No physical form at all.
infomorph.used_for: Lives in the mesh; embodies via teleoperation, drones, or resleeving. Has DUR/DR like any other morph but takes damage only from cyberattacks. Digital Speed: mesh tasks 25% faster. Cannot interact physically except through hosts or proxies. Always anthropomorphically 'small' for combat purposes.

flexbot.name: Flexbot
flexbot.short: A modular synthmorph made of interlocking units (Crafter, Fighter, Rogue, Wizard) that combine, separate, and reshape on demand.
flexbot.used_for: One module holds the ego and drives the rest. Combined modules pool their DUR, average their AV, and share pool boosts. (Dis)connecting takes a complex action + Integration Test. All synthmorph perks (immunity to bio threats, integral armor, pain filter) apply. Each module is small-sized alone.

Cortical Stack.short: Small armored implant at the base of the skull that continuously backs up your ego.
Cortical Stack.used_for: If your morph dies, recover the stack and your ego can be re-sleeved into a new body with memories intact up to the moment of death. Effectively transhuman immortality insurance.

Biomods.short: Genefixed baseline upgrades: disease resistance, longevity, enhanced healing, fitness.
Biomods.used_for: Standard on most biomorphs above flat. Doubles natural healing rate, immunizes against most natural diseases, and gives a long healthy lifespan.

Basic Biomods.short: The stripped-down version of biomods — disease resistance, decent healing, no lifespan boost.
Basic Biomods.used_for: Standard on pods. Better than a flat's biology, worse than a full biomorph's biomods.

Mesh Inserts.short: Cranial computer, radio, sensors, and AR display woven through your brain.
Mesh Inserts.used_for: Lets you mesh wirelessly (browse, message, run apps, share AR), record what you see/hear, and run a muse. Standard in nearly every morph. Without these, you need an ecto.

Basic Mesh Inserts.short: Lower-bandwidth, lower-storage version of mesh inserts. The pod/synth standard.
Basic Mesh Inserts.used_for: Same core functions (wireless mesh, AR, muse, basic recording) at reduced capacity. Still gets you online and useful.

Grip Pads.short: Setae-covered palms, fingertips, and feet that adhere to nearly any surface.
Grip Pads.used_for: +30 to climb anything reachable. Standard on bouncers and zero-g morphs.

Oxygen Reserve.short: An internal oxygen tank with auto-rebreather that kicks in during low/no atmosphere.
Oxygen Reserve.used_for: Survive 30 minutes in vacuum or toxic atmosphere without a suit. Standard on bouncers and other vacuum-rated morphs.

Vacuum Sealing.short: Skin and respiratory tract sealed against vacuum and pressure shifts.
Vacuum Sealing.used_for: Survives full vacuum exposure indefinitely (paired with oxygen reserve or alternate breathing). Standard on space-going morphs.

Hibernation.short: Voluntary metabolic shutdown to near-zero activity.
Hibernation.used_for: Trigger to enter true hibernation: no oxygen, food, or water needed for months. Ideal for long-duration space travel. Standard on hibernoid.

Toxin Filters.short: Implanted organ that neutralizes ingested or inhaled toxins.
Toxin Filters.used_for: +30 SOM Checks to resist poisons, drugs, and toxins. Reduces or eliminates damage from most chemical attacks.

Endocrine Control.short: Voluntary control over your own hormone production.
Endocrine Control.used_for: +10 WIL Checks to resist emotional manipulation and Provoke. Modulate fear, arousal, calm, and focus on demand.

Enhanced Hearing.short: Wider frequency range (infra- and ultra-sonic) and finer audio resolution.
Enhanced Hearing.used_for: +10 to hearing-based Perceive Tests. Hear what others can't, including silent dog whistles and structural creaks.

Enhanced Vision.short: Tetrachromatic color, wider frequency range (low IR/near-UV), and sharper focus.
Enhanced Vision.used_for: +10 to vision-based Perceive Tests. See in dim light, distinguish colors others can't, read distant detail.

Enhanced Senses.short: Combined upgrade pack for sight, hearing, smell, and touch.
Enhanced Senses.used_for: +10 to all sensory Perceive Tests. Common on security and investigation morphs.

Mental Speed.short: Accelerated cognition that lets you think and process several times faster than normal.
Mental Speed.used_for: Reduce timeframe of mental task actions by 50%. Stack with Insight pool spends for super-fast reasoning.

Eidetic Memory.short: Total recall of everything you have perceived since the implant was installed.
Eidetic Memory.used_for: +30 to memory-related COG Checks. Recall any conversation, image, or text verbatim.

Hyper-Linguist.short: Specialized language module that accelerates learning and use of natural languages.
Hyper-Linguist.used_for: +10 to INT Checks to grasp unknown languages. Halves time to learn a new language. Standard on menton.

Math Boost.short: Dedicated math co-processor in your skull.
Math Boost.used_for: +30 to Know and Technical Tests involving math, statistics, modeling, or geometry. Mental arithmetic at calculator speed.

Clean Metabolism.short: Body chemistry tuned to eliminate odors, waste, and dependence on common foods.
Clean Metabolism.used_for: No body odor, minimal waste, eats less, and stays presentable indefinitely. Common on sylphs and pleasure pods.

Enhanced Pheromones.short: Tunable pheromone production triggering attraction, trust, or calm in nearby people.
Enhanced Pheromones.used_for: +10 to Persuade and Provoke Tests on biomorphs in close range (a few meters). Common on sylphs and pleasure pods.

Medichines.short: Medical nanoswarm permanently resident in your body.
Medichines.used_for: Ignore 1 wound, heal at double speed, halve duration/effect of drugs and toxins. One of the most desirable biomorph upgrades.

Muscle Augmentation.used_for: +1d6 DV to melee damage, +10 SOM Checks for lifting and strength.

Enhanced Respiration.short: Modified lungs and bloodstream that handle thinner atmospheres and CO2-rich air.
Enhanced Respiration.used_for: Breathe in low-pressure or high-CO2 environments (Mars, mostly). Standard on rusters.

Access Jacks.short: Wired data ports — usually behind the ear or at the base of the skull.
Access Jacks.used_for: Direct cable connection to systems for higher bandwidth, immunity to wireless jamming, or stealthy non-mesh data transfer.

Cyberbrain.short: A digital brain replacing biological neurons. Standard in synthmorphs and pods.
Cyberbrain.used_for: Lets the morph run an uploaded ego natively, supports faster re-sleeving, hosts mnemonic memory and the puppet sock. Downside: it's a computer, so it can be hacked, infected, or subverted via Infosec attacks.

Mnemonic Augmentation.short: Memory-augmentation implant that records and time-indexes your sensory input.
Mnemonic Augmentation.used_for: Replay anything you've experienced. Common on synthmorphs, pods, and the menton. Often called Mnemonics in morph stat blocks.

Lidar.short: Light-based radar that maps surroundings in 3D out to a few hundred meters.
Lidar.used_for: See through smoke and darkness; build a real-time map of the area. Negates concealment from poor visibility.

Radar.short: Radio-frequency ranging that detects movement and structure through walls and obscurants.
Radar.used_for: Spot motion through walls and around obstacles. Penetrates smoke, fog, and most non-metal materials.

Industrial Armor.short: Built-in plating for synthmorphs and pods designed for hazardous work environments.
Industrial Armor.used_for: +6 Kinetic AV / +4 Energy AV. Stacks with worn armor. Standard on worker and security pods, savants.

Puppet Sock.short: Cyberbrain backdoor that lets a remote operator drive the morph as if their own body.
Puppet Sock.used_for: Allows teleoperation or AI control of the body. Standard on all cyberbrained morphs (synths and pods). Convenient — and a notorious attack surface for hackers.

Striking Looks.short: A face that turns heads even in a setting of sculpted beauty. (Level 1: synths/uplifts. Level 2: humanoid biomorphs.)
Striking Looks.used_for: +10 to Persuade and Provoke Tests where appearance matters. Standard on sylphs and many pleasure pods.

Exotic Morphology.short: Body plan substantially different from baseline humanoid (uplift, novacrab, swarmanoid, etc.).
Exotic Morphology.used_for: −10 per level to Integration Tests when first sleeving this body. Does NOT apply if it's your original morph type.

Pain Tolerance.short: Higher threshold for pain — wounds bother you less.
Pain Tolerance.used_for: Ignore 1 wound's −10 modifier per level. Max 3 wounds ignored when stacked with other pain-resistant effects. Can be Ego or Morph trait.

Digital Speed.name: Digital Speed
Digital Speed.short: Infomorph trait: think and act faster in pure-digital environments.
Digital Speed.used_for: While in pure-mesh / simulspace, gain +1 to mental action types; treat all infomorph actions as quick where physical would be complex. Drops to nil while teleoperating physical bodies.

_format.short: Movement rates list base/full distance in meters per action turn.
_format.used_for: Walker 4/20 means base move 4m (a free action) and full move 20m (a complex action). Some morphs list multiple types (e.g. Walker 2/8, Winged 8/40) because they can switch modes.

Walker.short: Legged locomotion — the default for humanoid morphs.
Walker.used_for: Most common type. Speeds vary with frame: standard humanoids 4/20, smaller morphs 4/12 or 2/8.

Roller.short: Wheel- or hoop-based ground motion using the morph's own body.
Roller.used_for: Slitheroids roll their segmented torso; arachnoids deploy mini-wheels. Faster than walking on smooth surfaces (usually 8/32 or 8/40).

Wheeled.short: Dedicated wheels or treads, deployed as needed.
Wheeled.used_for: Common on arachnoid morphs and bots. Fast on flat surfaces, struggles on rough terrain.

Thrust Vector.short: Compressed-air or ionic jets for propulsion in microgravity or in-atmosphere hover.
Thrust Vector.used_for: Standard on most synthmorphs and many bots. Lets you maneuver freely in zero-g without grabbing surfaces.

Hopper.used_for: Distinctive of swarmanoids, arachnoids, reapers. Can clear obstacles, change levels quickly.

Winged.used_for: Neo-avians and dragonfly bots have it; capable at 1 g with effort, much better in microgravity. Usually 8/32-8/40.

Snake.short: Sinuous slithering motion using lateral undulation.
Snake.used_for: Slitheroid morphs in their default form. Slower than rolling but works in tight spaces.

Swim.short: Aquatic propulsion — fins, jets, or limb-paddling.
Swim.used_for: Standard on neo-octopus and other water-adapted morphs.

Ionic.short: High-thrust ionic drive for sustained fast travel.
Ionic.used_for: Reaper combat morphs use this to close distance. Long-range fast acceleration.

Rotor.short: Helicopter-style rotor blades for vertical lift.
Rotor.used_for: Found on small drones and swarmanoid components. Hover and maneuver in atmosphere.

Weapons.short: Tools designed to inflict damage. EP2 weapons split into kinetic, beam, spray, seeker, melee, and implant types.
Weapons.used_for: Each weapon has a Damage Value (DV) rolled when you hit, plus traits (range, ammo, fire modes, armor piercing). Damage type determines which AV (Kinetic or Energy) reduces it.

Kinetic Weapons.short: Firearms, railguns, and projectile weapons. The most common ranged option.
Kinetic Weapons.used_for: Use Guns skill. Damage reduced by Kinetic AV. Single-Action, Burst Fire, and Full Auto modes (SA/BF/FA). Smartlinked rounds and frangible/AP variants change behavior.

Beam Weapons.used_for: Use Guns skill. Damage reduced by Energy AV. Usually silent and recoilless. Many ignore some armor or have continuous-fire modes.

Spray Weapons.short: Flamers, chemical sprayers, freezers, and stunners that project a cone or stream.
Spray Weapons.used_for: Use Guns skill. Cover an area; harder to dodge but limited range. Variants split between Kinetic and Energy AV.

Seeker Weapons.short: Smart micromissiles and mini-rockets with onboard guidance.
Seeker Weapons.used_for: Use Guns skill. Fire-and-forget; harder for the target to dodge. Various warheads (HEAP, plasma, EMP, smoke).

Melee Weapons.short: Knives, swords, clubs, axes, vibroblades, monofilament weapons.
Melee Weapons.used_for: Use Melee skill. Damage reduced by Kinetic AV. Many are concealable; some have Reach or Armor-Piercing.

Implant Weapons.short: Built-in weapons grown into a morph: claws, retractable blades, shock organs, beak attacks.
Implant Weapons.used_for: Always available, hard to detect, usually impossible to disarm. Use Melee (or Exotic) skill.

Armor.short: Worn or implanted protection. Every armor has two ratings: Kinetic AV and Energy AV, written K/E (e.g. 8/6).
Armor.used_for: When you take damage, subtract the appropriate AV (kinetic or energy) from incoming DV. Synthmorphs have built-in armor (Light Frame 6/4, Medium 8/6, Heavy 12/10). Worn armor stacks with implant armor up to a max.

Drugs.short: Chemical compounds for combat boosts, social leverage, healing, and recreation.
Drugs.used_for: Each drug has an onset, duration, application method (oral/inhaled/injected/etc.), and effect. Many give pool boosts capped at +5. Common biomorph use; synths usually can't metabolize them.

Nanotech.short: Programmable nanoswarms — clouds of microscopic robots that perform a designated task.
Nanotech.used_for: Categories include healer/fixer, scout/spy, guardian/disabler, cleaner, smart-dust. Use Hardware: Nanotech or Interface to deploy and direct.

Bots.short: Autonomous drones and robots run by ALIs or controlled by a remote operator.
Bots.used_for: Range from insect-sized (speck, smart hawk) to combat-grade (guardian angel, automech). Each has its own stats and Pilot/Interface use.

Vehicles.used_for: Roll Pilot: [field] to operate. Have own armor, DUR, and weapon mounts. Some morphs (flexbots, arachnoids) are themselves vehicle-scale.

Sensors.short: Radar, lidar, t-ray, electrical sense, nanoscopic vision, biometric scanners.
Sensors.used_for: Defeat darkness, smoke, concealment, and biometric spoofing. Often integrated as ware in morphs, also as standalone gear.

Tools.short: Repair kits, tool kits, fabbers, utility tools, specialist instruments.
Tools.used_for: Many tests require a tool kit (no tools = −10 to −30 modifier). Fabbers build other items from blueprints; bigger fabber, bigger item.

Tactical.short: Combat-support gear: TacNet apps, smartlinks, smart cuffs, smart dust, scopes, exoskeletons.
Tactical.used_for: TacNet shares sensor and team data in real time. Smartlinks and scopes give modifier bonuses on attack rolls.

Communications.short: Ectos, radio boosters, satphones, signal jammers, anonymizers, private servers.
Communications.used_for: Provide mesh access without inserts, extend range, hide identity, or block enemy signals. The ecto is the standard exterior smartphone.

Survival.short: Vacsuits, breathers, pressure tents, healing sprays, survival rations, magboots.
Survival.used_for: Keep you alive in vacuum, deep ocean, hostile atmospheres, or simply on long expeditions. Many morphs already have some of this baked in.

Stealth.short: Chameleon cloaks, anonymizers, skinflex disguises, microbugs, signal jammers, smart dust.
Stealth.used_for: Defeat detection, conceal identity, or hide presence — from sensors and from other transhumans. Big bonuses to Infiltrate.

gear_avail_cost.short: Every gear item has two ratings written as Complexity/GP, e.g. Min/1 or Maj/R/3. Complexity = how hard to find or fabricate; GP = how much it costs from your starting Gear Points.

availability.Min: Minimal complexity — household, mass-market, common everywhere. Easy to scrounge or fab.
availability.Mod: Moderate complexity — professional or specialist gear. Available legally in most habitats.
availability.Maj: Major complexity — high-end, restricted, or dangerous. Often requires legitimate justification or black-market connections.
availability.Top: Top complexity — bleeding-edge, prototype, or extremely restricted. GM-discretion to acquire.

restricted.R: Suffix 'R' on Complexity means the item is restricted, regulated, or illegal in many polities. Possession may attract authorities.

gp_cost.1: 1 GP — Minor item. Most common gear at this tier.
gp_cost.2: 2 GP — Moderate item. Specialist apps, mid-grade ware, midrange drones.
gp_cost.3: 3 GP — Major item. Premium ware (medichines, neurachem, healing vat), heavy weapons, vehicles.

anonymizer.name: Anonymizer
anonymizer.short: App that masks your mesh ID and obscures your network presence.
anonymizer.used_for: Stops casual tracing. Makes you a non-trivial target for Research/Infosec attempts to identify you.

ecto.name: Ecto
ecto.short: Exterior smart-fabric computer — your phone, mesh terminal, and AR rig if you lack Mesh Inserts.
ecto.used_for: Full mesh access, AR display, app/muse host. Most non-morph-implanted characters carry one.

mesh-amplifier.name: Mesh-Amplifier
mesh-amplifier.short: Portable booster that increases your mesh range and bandwidth.
mesh-amplifier.used_for: Maintain quality mesh links across larger areas or through interference.

private-server.name: Private Server
private-server.short: A dedicated server you control, hostable anywhere or hosted by a service.
private-server.used_for: Run your own infomorph instances, host secure data, anchor forks, store backups outside corporate or state systems.

vpn-app.name: VPN App
vpn-app.short: Creates an encrypted virtual private network between participants.
vpn-app.used_for: Secure group comms; resists casual eavesdropping and traffic analysis.

satphone.name: Satphone
satphone.used_for: Stay in contact when out of mesh range — exoplanet surfaces, deep wilderness, off-grid habitats.

radio-booster.name: Radio Booster
radio-booster.short: Increases radio range to 25 km (or 250 km with relay).
radio-booster.used_for: Long-range comms across open terrain and habitat exteriors.

anti-glare-goggles.name: Anti-Glare Goggles
anti-glare-goggles.short: Optical filter that suppresses bright-light glare and dazzlers.
anti-glare-goggles.used_for: Negate glare modifiers from sunlight, spotlights, flash, or dazzler weapons.

breadcrumb-positioning-system.name: Breadcrumb Positioning System
breadcrumb-positioning-system.short: Drops a trail of tiny radio motes as you move.
breadcrumb-positioning-system.used_for: Lets you retrace your path or be located by allies, even without GPS or mesh coverage.

microbug.name: Microbug
microbug.short: Micro-sized camera and audio recorder, often disguised as a speck of dust or fiber.
microbug.used_for: Surveillance — plant, leave behind, retrieve. Streams back to your mesh.

privacy-shield.name: Privacy Shield
privacy-shield.short: Field that disrupts nearby surveillance feeds.
privacy-shield.used_for: Block visual and audio recording within an area. Detected by counter-surveillance.

smart-dust.name: Smart Dust
smart-dust.short: Cloud of microscopic sensor motes that drift and adhere to surfaces.
smart-dust.used_for: Wide-area passive surveillance — temperature, motion, sound, low-rez video.

tool-kit.name: Tool Kit
tool-kit.short: Portable hardware/repair kit suited to one Hardware field.
tool-kit.used_for: Without the right tools, technical tests take −10 to −30. With a kit, you can attempt the test at normal modifier.

cold-suit.name: Cold Suit
cold-suit.short: Insulated, heated suit for sub-zero environments.
cold-suit.used_for: Survive extended exposure on icy worlds, Europa surface, low-temp gatecrash sites.

heat-suit.name: Heat Suit
heat-suit.short: Refrigerated, reflective suit for high-temperature environments.
heat-suit.used_for: Survive extended exposure on Venus surface, near molten flows, fires.

exoskeleton.name: Exoskeleton
exoskeleton.short: Worn powered frame that amplifies strength and load-bearing.
exoskeleton.used_for: Carry heavy gear, work in high gravity, supplement weak morphs. Adds SOM bonus and lift capacity.

gatecrasher-kit.name: Gatecrasher's Kit
gatecrasher-kit.short: Bundled survival and sampling kit for new-world expeditions.
gatecrasher-kit.used_for: Tools for documenting an unfamiliar exoplanet — sensor suite, sample containers, emergency beacon.

healing-vat.name: Healing Vat
healing-vat.short: Coffin-sized regrowth tank for serious biomorph repair.
healing-vat.used_for: Heal/cure biomorphs, restore lost limbs, install/remove implants, customize a morph. Slow (hours to days) but very powerful.

magboots.name: Magboots
magboots.short: Electromagnetic boots that grip metal surfaces.
magboots.used_for: Walk on hulls, station exteriors, and in microgravity environments.

solar-panel.name: Solar Panel
solar-panel.short: Foldable panel that powers small gear from sunlight.
solar-panel.used_for: Keep your kit running on long expeditions without an external grid.

smart-clothing.name: Smart Clothing
smart-clothing.short: Reconfigurable smart-fabric outfit that changes color, texture, and cut.
smart-clothing.used_for: Shift wardrobe in seconds; gives +10 to Infiltrate when blending in, +30 when stationary and covered.

survival-rations.name: Survival Rations
survival-rations.short: Compact nutrient bars and water purification for long trips.
survival-rations.used_for: Keep biomorph going for weeks in the wilderness or vacuum-rated containers.

disposable-mesh-accounts.name: Disposable Mesh Accounts
disposable-mesh-accounts.short: Pre-made burner mesh identities with light scrubbed history.
disposable-mesh-accounts.used_for: Conduct one transaction or short identity-shifted operation, then discard. Less convincing than a Fake Ego ID.

fake-ego-id.name: Fake Ego ID
fake-ego-id.short: Forged identity package — ID, backstory, biometric markers, and its own rep scores.

lockpick-array.name: Lockpick Array

scrounged-armor-vest.name: Scrounged Armor Vest

attack.short: Roll d100 vs your skill (Guns or Melee) + modifiers. Target rolls opposed Fray (or Fray/2 against guns) or Melee to dodge/parry. Higher successful roll wins.

damage.short: Damage Value (DV) is the dice you roll on a hit — usually a weapon's listed DV plus any bonuses (margin of success, superior result, weapon traits). Subtract the target's relevant Armor Value, then apply to DUR.

armor.short: Every armor item has two values: Kinetic AV (vs bullets, kinetic, melee) and Energy AV (vs lasers, plasma, fire). Written K/E (e.g. 8/6). Subtract the AV matching the incoming damage type from DV before applying.

wounds.short: Any single hit dealing damage equal to or above Wound Threshold (DUR/5) inflicts 1 wound. Each wound: cumulative −10 to action tests, −1 Initiative, and forces a SOM Check or you fall. At total damage = DUR you're unconscious (biomorph) or crashed (synth); at DR you're dead/wrecked.

trauma.short: Any single stress hit equal to or above Trauma Threshold (LUC/5) inflicts 1 trauma. Each trauma: cumulative −10 to actions, −1 Initiative, forces a WIL Check or you're stunned. At total stress = LUC you suffer a breakdown (1d6 hours catatonic, gain a Mental Disorder); at IR your mind is permanently lost.

initiative.short: Initiative stat = (REF + INT) / 5. Each turn roll 1d6 + Initiative; high roll goes first. Spend 1 Vigor (any action) or 1 Insight (mental/mesh only) to act first regardless of roll.

action_economy.short: A 3-second action turn allows ONE of: 1 complex action + 1 quick action, OR 1 task action + 1 quick action, OR up to 3 quick actions. Plus unlimited automatic actions. Basic movement (base move) is automatic; full move uses a complex action.

criticals.short: Any double on the d100 (00, 11, 22, ..., 99) is a critical. Roll of 00 is always a critical success regardless of target; 99 is always a critical failure. Crits give GM-discretion bonuses or penalties beyond the standard result.

superior_results.short: 33/66 rule: a successful roll of 33 or higher is a superior success (more damage, extra detail, etc.); 66+ is a double superior. A failure of 66 or less is a superior failure; 33 or less is a double superior failure. See tests.superior_results.

healing.short: Biomorphs heal damage with rest, healing spray, medichines, paramedic Medicine Tests, or a healing vat. Synthmorphs require Hardware: Robotics repairs, fixer swarms, or an automech. Mental damage heals via Medicine: Psychosurgery, downtime, motivational milestones, and Moxie spends.

mp.short: Morph Points — your chargen budget for buying a starting morph (Step 12). Default 6 MP, plus your Resources trait level.
mp.used_for: Spend MP on: (1) one or more morphs, (2) extra morph traits (positive cost MP, negative refund up to 6 MP), (3) extra gear (1 MP per Minor, 2 per Moderate, 3 per Major). Leftover MP converts to Flex points at 2 MP = 1 Flex, max 3 Flex. Those Flex points reset the next time you resleeve.

rules_notes.starting_default: 6 MP, increased by your Resources trait level.
rules_notes.first_morph_minimum: If buying more than one morph, the first must cost 1+ MP (a 0-MP morph counts as 1 MP when bought after the first).
rules_notes.negative_trait_cap: No more than 6 MP worth of negative morph traits.
rules_notes.flex_conversion: Leftover MP -> Flex at 2:1, max 3 Flex. Resets on next resleeve.

chargen.used_for: Build the character through 13 steps: lifepath, aptitudes, skills, morph, gear, motivations. Changes are immediate and the preview pane updates live.

play.short: Play mode — wizard is locked, sheet is interactive.
play.used_for: Track current pool spends, wounds, and stress during a session. Switch to Chargen to edit lifepath / mechanics again.

career.used_for: Each career carries gear that fits its job — a Hacker gets ecto + specialist apps; a Soldier gets armor + assault weapon. You may swap items with GM approval.

habitat-ops.name: Habitat Ops
habitat-ops.setting: Habitats are artificial space environments — torus and cylinder spin habs, asteroid hollows, aerostats in Venusian cloud, cluster modules — and habitat ops is the living infrastructure that keeps them alive: life support, air mix and recycling, hull integrity, spin balance, thermal management, environmental equilibrium. In a habitat, one fire or one decompression event can kill everyone aboard, so the people who know hab ops are the people who notice trouble first.
habitat-ops.hooks: the engineer who smells the air mix going off before any alert fires; the systems chief who survived a hab failure and refuses to let it happen again; the maintenance veteran who knows every duct, every quirk, every system by touch.

hab-ops.name: Hab Ops
hab-ops.setting: Short for Habitat Ops — same knowledge, same field. Life support, air, recycling, spin, hull, thermals. The discipline that keeps your station from killing everyone aboard.
hab-ops.hooks: the engineer who smells the air mix going off before any alert fires; the systems chief who survived a hab failure and refuses to let it happen again; the maintenance veteran who knows every duct, every quirk, every system by touch.

flight-crew-ops.name: Flight Crew Ops
flight-crew-ops.setting: The professional knowledge of running a spacecraft as crew, not just piloting it: cargo handling, passenger procedures, docking protocols, customs and inspection routines, fuel and life support logistics, comms discipline, microgravity safety drills. Anyone who has worked the lanes between habs knows this work intimately.
flight-crew-ops.hooks: the long-haul crewer who has seen every kind of customs scam; the steward who can defuse a passenger panic in microgravity; the bosun who reads a ship's mood the way others read a room.

gatecrashing.name: Gatecrashing
gatecrashing.setting: Pandora gates are alien wormholes — five known to transhumanity — that connect the Solar System to exoplanets across the galaxy. Gatecrashing is the profession (and lifestyle) of going through them: first-in protocols, gear loads for unknown environments, gate-time logistics, return-window discipline, hostile xenoecology, anomaly identification. Often lethal, occasionally world-changing.
gatecrashing.hooks: the veteran of a first-in op that went wrong on the far side; the xenosurveyor who has walked more exoplanets than habitats; the contract gatecrasher between expeditions, restless and bored on the wrong side of the wormhole.

terraforming.name: Terraforming
terraforming.setting: Mars is the only large-scale terraforming project in the system, and the political fights around it are bitter — settle the surface, claim the land, change the air, decide who Mars is for. Terraforming knowledge covers atmospheric chemistry, ecopoesis, large-scale climate engineering, microbial seeding, and the long-game economics of remaking a world over centuries.
terraforming.hooks: the Tharsis Terraforming Office veteran with conflicted loyalties; the Barsoomian agronomist who thinks the project belongs to Martians, not hypercorps; the exoplanet ecologist asking whether we should be doing this at all.

spacecraft.name: Spacecraft
spacecraft.setting: Knowledge of spacecraft as systems: types of drive (chemical, fusion, antimatter, ion), ship classes (tugs, shuttles, freighters, gunships, exploration vessels), life support architecture, registries, drive signatures, who builds what. The 'spaceship models' interest in p53. Most transhumans live and die aboard them.
spacecraft.hooks: the ship-nut who can identify a hull by drive plume; the ex-crew who knows every quirk of a particular class; the smuggler who can tell a customs cruiser from a courier at a hundred kilometers.

titan-machines.name: TITAN Machines
titan-machines.setting: The TITANs were transhumanity's military seed AIs that achieved hard takeoff during the Fall, devastated Earth, and then vanished — leaving behind contaminated zones, alien architecture, the exsurgent virus, and machines that still occasionally wake up. Knowledge of TITAN tech means recognizing their handiwork: weapons, infrastructure, code, fab patterns, the wrong kind of symmetry. Most of it is lethal, contagious, or both. Specialists are vanishingly rare and usually compartmented.
titan-machines.hooks: the salvager who survived a TITAN site and won't talk about why; the Firewall asset who studies what no one else will touch; the engineer who recognizes TITAN signatures in things they shouldn't be in.

morph-design.name: Morph Design
morph-design.setting: Morphs are the bodies — biomorphs grown in exowombs, synthmorphs assembled in shops, pods stitched from biological and synthetic parts, infomorphs that are pure code. Morph design is the work of specifying them: genelines, neural architecture, bioware suites, aesthetic and functional choices, baseline traits. Every body you've ever sleeved was designed by someone.
morph-design.hooks: the genehacker who builds bespoke sleeves for clients with strange needs; the ex-corporate designer who fled with their proprietary lines; the pod-shaper whose work blurs the lines between art and biology.

body-bank-ops.name: Body Bank Ops
body-bank-ops.setting: Body banks are where morphs get cycled — stored, refurbished, sold, leased, repossessed. They're hospitals, mortuaries, garages, and warehouses at once. Knowledge of body bank ops covers vat schedules, ego-sleeving procedures, morph availability and pricing, biomonitoring, escrow protocols, and the paperwork of moving minds between bodies. Adjacent industries: insurance, ego transfer, organ trade, illegal flesh markets.
body-bank-ops.hooks: the body bank tech who has watched a thousand resleeves and seen a few go wrong; the broker who knows which morphs are clean and which have hidden mods; the ex-Goules operative trying to leave the illegal morph trade behind.

ego-hunting.name: Ego Hunting
ego-hunting.setting: An ego is a person — the mind-pattern that gets backed up, transferred, and resleeved into a new morph. Ego hunting is the trade of tracking egos across the Solar System and exoplanets: bounty work for skipped indentures, recovery of forknapped backups, locating someone who keeps egocasting away. Half investigation, half network expertise; usually adjacent to crime regardless of which side hires you.
ego-hunting.hooks: the freelance ego hunter who works both sides; the Firewall asset who quietly recovers contaminated egos before they wake up; the Nine Lives defector hunting the syndicate that owns their backup.

mind-hacks.name: Mind Hacks
mind-hacks.setting: Psychosurgery — the cognitive science of rewriting minds. Memory editing, behavior masking, hidden knowledge implants, interrogation, deep learning, personality alteration. Legitimate uses (therapy, skill imprints, trauma healing) sit next to terrifying ones (forced compliance, false memories, mind control). Most muses can perform minor psychosurgery; full procedures take specialists. Mind hacks is the knowledge side of that whole landscape.
mind-hacks.hooks: the ex-psychosurgeon haunted by who they edited and why; the underground specialist who runs anonymous trauma clinics; the Firewall asset who studies illegal edits to recognize them in others.

memetics.name: Memetics
memetics.setting: Memes are weaponized ideas — propaganda, narrative warfare, viral framing, social-engineering campaigns designed to reshape populations. In Eclipse Phase 2 memetics is treated seriously enough to be listed as an x-risk in its own right. Every faction runs memetic ops; every habitat is downstream of someone's narrative. Memeticists design, deploy, and counter these campaigns.
memetics.hooks: the ex-Consortium memeticist who defected and now runs counter-narratives; the Barsoomian propagandist who turned a colony anti-corporate one slogan at a time; the analyst who reads social trends like weather and predicts the next mass panic.

nanofacturing.name: Nanofacturing
nanofacturing.setting: Nanofabrication is how almost everything gets made in EP2 — molecular 3D printing from feedstock, driven by blueprints. Nanofacturing as a profession covers the industrial side: factory-scale fabbers, hive arrays, feedstock logistics, blueprint libraries, quality control, the politics of who controls which designs. The Argonauts run an open-source repo called PrintLib; hypercorps fight tooth and nail over proprietary blueprints.
nanofacturing.hooks: the factory veteran who has run every kind of fabber line; the PrintLib contributor smuggling blueprints to autonomist habs; the corporate compliance officer hunting unauthorized prints.

nanotechnology.name: Nanotechnology
nanotechnology.setting: The science underneath nanofabrication — molecular machines, swarms, hives, medichines, gray-goo theory, the difference between a useful nano and a runaway one. Most consumer-facing nanotech is mundane (autocooks, fixer swarms, medichines), but the field also includes weapons-grade and TITAN-derived horrors. Listed as an x-risk for a reason.
nanotechnology.hooks: the nanotech researcher who has signed too many NDAs; the swarm specialist who builds custom hives for outer-system clients; the recovery worker who scrubs nanocontamination out of habitats and dreams about it.

bioconservativism.name: Bioconservativism
bioconservativism.setting: A political stance opposing core transhuman tech: resleeving, uploading, AGI, uplifts, radical augmentation. Pre-Fall it was fringe; the destruction of Earth catalyzed it into a major movement. The Jovian Republic is its institutional home — a militarized polity that bans most transhuman tech outright. Knowing bioconservativism means knowing its arguments, its factions, its sympathizers in unexpected places, and its terror tactics.
bioconservativism.hooks: the ex-Jovian who left over an argument they still half-believe; the Firewall asset who infiltrates biocon cells; the negotiator who has actually had productive talks with bioconservatives and surprised everyone.

hypercorp-politics.name: Hypercorp Politics
hypercorp-politics.setting: Hypercorps are the post-national giants — they run the Planetary Consortium, own most of Mars and the inner system, and operate proprietary habitats, body banks, gates, and entire industries. Hypercorp politics is the knowledge of who holds which seats, who is feuding with whom (Omnicor versus Starware, Pathfinder versus TerraGenesis), which corps Oversight is sniffing around, where Project Ozma is rumored to operate.
hypercorp-politics.hooks: the ex-corporate exec who knows where every body is buried; the Consortium-trained negotiator who plays the long game; the journalist who maps the dotted lines between boardrooms.

political-science.name: Political Science
political-science.setting: Knowledge of how transhuman polities function: the Lunar-Lagrange Alliance's council voting, the Planetary Consortium's hypercorp blocs, the Autonomist Alliance's four points of unity, the Titanian Commonwealth's micro-democracy, the Jovian Republic's military rule. In a system with this many ideologies actively in conflict, political theory is survival knowledge.
political-science.hooks: the academic whose work gets quoted by people on every side; the diplomat with too many citizenships; the Firewall analyst who reads polity dynamics like weather patterns.

uplift-culture.name: Uplift Culture
uplift-culture.setting: Uplifts are non-human animals raised to sapience — neo-octopuses, neo-ravens, neo-gorillas, neo-chimps and bonobos, neo-orangutans, and others. Each species has its own evolving culture, internal politics, and ongoing struggle for rights. Knowledge of uplift culture covers their histories, their art, their factional fights (Sapients vs. Mercurials), the Kisilev open-source uplift genetic library, and the daily reality of living transhuman without being human.
uplift-culture.hooks: the uplift advocate working political channels; the neo-avian artist drawing on a cultural inheritance only a generation old; the transhuman ally who actually listens.

uplift-rights.name: Uplift Rights
uplift-rights.setting: The legal and political fight for uplift autonomy — opposing indenture contracts, owning their own genome, voting, parental rights for genetically-modified offspring. Status varies wildly by polity: outer system mostly respects uplifts as full sapients, inner system treats many as property or second-class citizens. Adjacent to AGI rights and the broader Mercurial movement.
uplift-rights.hooks: the uplift-rights lawyer fighting indenture cases habitat by habitat; the Mercurial organizer who lost family to forced sterilization; the ally with hypercorp connections quietly leaking documents.

black-markets.name: Black Markets
black-markets.setting: Every banned good, every restricted service, every illegal morph or ego has a market somewhere — and habitats run on these markets more than their councils admit. Knowing the black markets means knowing brokers, fences, dead-drop sites, encrypted auction houses, current prices on contraband morphs, illegal AGIs, weapons-grade nano, narcoalgorithms, and forknapped egos.
black-markets.hooks: the broker who can source almost anything for the right rep; the ex-cop turned consultant who knows which fences talk to which cops; the smuggler retired into legitimate trade who can still make introductions.

xp-dealers.name: XP Dealers
xp-dealers.setting: XP is experience playback — recorded sensory streams of someone else's life, played back through your mesh inserts as their own felt experience. Legal XP is entertainment and journalism; illegal XP includes torture recordings, murder logs, illegal sex, and underground combat. XP dealers are the people who move the recordings, both clean and dirty. Underground XP is the ugly half of the trade.
xp-dealers.hooks: the XP dealer who knows which recordings are real; the recovering XP addict who can still spot a fresh feed; the journalist who uses XP to expose what nobody else can prove.

underground-xp.name: Underground XP
underground-xp.setting: The illegal XP scene — snuff feeds, torture recordings, illegal combat streams, leaked private moments, footage from TITAN-contaminated zones. The dark mesh trades it constantly; Firewall watches because exsurgent virus has been seeded through XP before. Knowing the underground XP scene is knowing who deals what, which feeds are real, and which collectors are dangerous to meet.
underground-xp.hooks: the ex-collector who burned their library and can't quite forget it; the dark-mesh investigator hunting a specific recording; the addict working their way out one substitution at a time.

cartel-politics.name: Cartel Politics
cartel-politics.setting: Knowledge of the major criminal syndicates — Nine Lives (soul-trafficking out of Legba), the Night Cartel (extortion, nano-piracy, gambling), Pax Familae (Claudia Ambelina's fork-clones running fraud system-wide), the Hidden Concern, the ID Crew, Pirates. Who controls which routes, which feuds are active, which truces are nominal, who Firewall is willing to deal with.
cartel-politics.hooks: the analyst who maps cartel territories on borrowed mesh time; the Firewall asset who runs cartel informants; the ex-soldier who used to work cartel security and walked.

cartels.name: Cartels
cartels.setting: Same field as Cartel Politics — knowledge of the major post-Fall criminal syndicates. Nine Lives (soul-trafficking), Night Cartel (nano-piracy and racketeering), Pax Familae (fork-clones running fraud), Pirates, the Triads. Each cartel has its own territories, rituals, and product lines.
cartels.hooks: the analyst who maps cartel territories on borrowed mesh time; the Firewall asset who runs cartel informants; the ex-soldier who used to work cartel security and walked.

racketeering.name: Racketeering
racketeering.setting: The professional practice of organized crime — protection rackets, extortion, kickback structures, money laundering through legitimate hypercorp fronts, intimidation campaigns. In the Solar System this includes Earth-style mob tactics adapted for habitats: control the airlocks, control the body banks, control the rep economy in your zone.
racketeering.hooks: the enforcer who is tired of breaking fingers; the accountant who launders for a cartel and hates themself; the ex-mark who learned the trade from the inside and uses it for revenge.

smuggling.name: Smuggling
smuggling.setting: Moving contraband — weapons, illegal morphs, forknapped egos, hostile nano, banned XP, restricted blueprints — between habitats and across polity borders. Routes through the Belt, slingshot transits around Jupiter, gate-runs, customs evasion, fence networks at the destination. Half logistics, half social engineering. Every smuggler eventually deals with cartels even if they tried not to.
smuggling.hooks: the captain who runs a clean ship and asks no questions; the route specialist who knows every customs blind spot in the inner system; the ex-smuggler turned Firewall courier.

triads.name: Triads
triads.setting: Long-running East Asian-origin crime syndicates that survived the Fall and adapted aggressively to the post-Fall economy. Heavy in drugs, prostitution and trafficking, extortion, nanofab piracy, gambling, and darknet operations. Often present themselves as legitimate hypercorps; in reality most habitats with a Triad presence know exactly what they are.
triads.hooks: the Triad-adjacent fixer who can open any door for a price; the ex-soldier who left and is still looking over their shoulder; the investigator building a case nobody is brave enough to prosecute.

fencing.name: Fencing
fencing.setting: The trade of moving stolen goods — morphs, gear, blueprints, art, data, egos. A fence knows valuations, which buyers will not ask questions, how to wipe identifying nano-tags off an item, how to launder physical objects through legitimate-looking trade flows. Adjacent to black markets and racketeering.
fencing.hooks: the fence who refuses certain kinds of merchandise on principle; the appraiser-turned-fence who can spot a fake at a glance; the ex-cop who knows every fence in their station by reputation.

security-ops.name: Security Ops
security-ops.setting: Habitat security, corporate security, hypercorp private armies, contracted Direct Action and Ultimate Security personnel. Security ops covers patrol patterns, surveillance design, response protocols, K&R procedures, threat assessment, and the everyday rhythm of guarding a space full of people. Different from military ops — security defends specific assets and locations, not territory or polity.
security-ops.hooks: the ex-corporate security lead who saw too much; the contractor between gigs; the systems chief who designs perimeters and dreams about the gap they can't quite close.

military-ops.name: Military Ops
military-ops.setting: Polity-scale armed force — the Jovian Republic's fleet, the Titanian Fleet, hypercorp militaries, the wars before and during the Fall, the Seventeen-Minute War around Jupiter, the modern Cold War between inner and outer system. Doctrine, logistics, strategy, who has what fleet, how they fight. Most veterans of actual combat lived through the Fall.
military-ops.hooks: the Fall veteran who never quite came home; the Jovian defector with operational knowledge; the autonomist militia organizer studying every doctrine they can find.

police-ops.name: Police Ops
police-ops.setting: Habitat policing — investigations, evidence procedures, arrest protocols, jurisdictional politics, the relationship between police and the hypercorp or polity that funds them. Wildly different by habitat: Consortium habs have heavy surveillance and corporate-aligned police; anarchist habs have community defense and no cops at all; Jovian habs are essentially militarized.
police-ops.hooks: the ex-detective who left over a case they were told to drop; the internal affairs investigator with too many enemies; the autonomist mediator who has tried to do the job without a badge.

spycraft.name: Spycraft
spycraft.setting: Tradecraft for the EP2 era — running assets, dead drops via mesh, ego-disguise via resleeving and psychosurgery, fork-based parallel ops, exfil via egocasting, dealing with universal surveillance by exploiting its gaps. Every major polity has its services. Project Ozma is the spookiest of them. Firewall is technically not an intelligence service but operates like one.
spycraft.hooks: the burned officer who knows too much about three services; the ex-Ozma asset who walked away with files; the Firewall sentinel running long-cover in an enemy polity.

conflict-zones.name: Conflict Zones
conflict-zones.setting: Active warzones in the Solar System and on exoplanets — the TQZ (TITAN Quarantine Zone) on Mars, contested Belt habitats, Earth's interdiction satellites and the surface beneath them, exoplanet first-in operations that went wrong, ongoing skirmishes between polities. Knowing conflict zones means knowing the rules of engagement, who currently holds what, how to move through, and what to never touch.
conflict-zones.hooks: the ex-mercenary who has worked half the zones in the system; the journalist who reports from the inside; the survivor of an exoplanet evacuation who still has the scars.

mercenary-groups.name: Mercenary Groups
mercenary-groups.setting: Private military contractors — Direct Action, Ultimate Security, dozens of smaller outfits, autonomist defense collectives that function as mercs when contracted out. Who fights for who, which outfits will take what kinds of contracts, current rosters, reputations. The Morningstar Constellation in particular relies heavily on contracted muscle.
mercenary-groups.hooks: the ex-Direct Action operative who has seen the contracts from the inside; the fixer who brokers between mercs and clients; the merc commander trying to keep their people out of the worst jobs.

bodyguarding.name: Bodyguarding
bodyguarding.setting: Close-protection work in a setting where the protectee can be killed, forknapped, ego-stolen, body-swapped, psychosurgically attacked, or memed into self-harm. Modern bodyguarding integrates mesh security, backup discipline, morph-design considerations, threat modeling against psychosurgical attack, and the boring fundamentals — sightlines, routes, drills.
bodyguarding.hooks: the close-protection professional who has lost a principal once and never again; the Firewall asset working bodyguard cover; the personal security lead trying to retire and unable to stop noticing exits.

forensics.name: Forensics
forensics.setting: Investigative science in the EP2 era — biological forensics (autopsies, DNA, biochem), but also digital forensics on cyberbrains and mesh devices, ego-state analysis, psychosurgery detection, morph-history reconstruction, exsurgent-contamination screening. Adjacent to Medicine: Forensics but the Know variant covers context, history, and method literacy rather than direct procedural work.
forensics.hooks: the forensic investigator who can read a crime scene like a story; the digital forensicist who hunts modified memories; the ex-cop consultant who knows the right questions to ask the body.

astrobiology.name: Astrobiology
astrobiology.setting: The science of life beyond Earth. In EP2 this is no longer speculative: exoplanet ecosystems are sampled regularly through the pandora gates, dead alien civilizations like the Iktomi have been catalogued, and the Factors confirm intelligent extraterrestrial life exists. Astrobiology covers biosignatures, alien biochemistry, exoplanet ecology, and the comparative biology of what little we have actually met.
astrobiology.hooks: the field researcher who has walked more exoplanet biomes than colleagues have read about; the Argonaut studying Factor samples in secret; the contamination specialist who screens returning gatecrashers.

xenoarcheology.name: Xenoarcheology
xenoarcheology.setting: The archaeology of extinct alien civilizations. Iktomi ruins on Droplet, Echo, Haplopelma, Sunrise. Older sites, some 10,000 years old, some far older. Pandora gates themselves are alien artifacts. Xenoarcheologists try to read the cataclysms that killed those species — which is, transhumans hope, not the same cataclysm coming for them.
xenoarcheology.hooks: the field archaeologist who has spent more time on exoplanets than at home; the obsessive who believes Iktomi died from something still out there; the museum specialist quietly cataloguing things the public should never see.

cognitive-science.name: Cognitive Science
cognitive-science.setting: The science of mind in an era where minds run on cortical stacks, get edited by psychosurgery, fork into copies, merge back together, and run as infomorphs on servers. Cognitive science underpins everything from resleeving therapy to AGI design to memetic warfare to interrogation protocols. Sits next to neuroscience, psychology, AI research, and the dark arts of mind hacking.
cognitive-science.hooks: the researcher whose papers get cited by people they would never agree with; the psychosurgeon thinking through what consciousness really is; the AGI-rights advocate with a neuroscience background.

field-science.name: Field Science
field-science.setting: The professional practice of doing science outside the lab — expedition logistics, sample collection in hostile environments, in-situ analysis, hardening instruments for vacuum or extreme gravity, gatecrashing scientific protocols, working with limited gear under time pressure. Different from any specific science: field science is the meta-skill of running a science operation in the wild.
field-science.hooks: the expedition lead who has lost colleagues and learned from it; the gatecrasher with a science budget; the freelance researcher who works contract-to-contract on the system's frontier.

physiology.name: Physiology
physiology.setting: Knowledge of how transhuman bodies work — biomorphs, pods, uplifts, the modded and the baseline. Implants and bioware interactions, oxygen and energy economy across morph types, the differences between species of uplift, how a synthmorph's mind-body interface differs from a biomorph's. Foundational for medics, body bank workers, and morph designers alike.
physiology.hooks: the physiologist who specializes in uplifts and notices what other doctors miss; the trauma medic with deep cross-morph experience; the bioengineer trying to design a body for an environment nobody has lived in yet.

psychometrics.name: Psychometrics
psychometrics.setting: The measurement side of cognitive science — testing for sanity, screening for personality alteration, detecting psychosurgical edits, evaluating fork-merge stability, screening returning gatecrashers for exsurgent infection. Used by therapists, by Firewall, by corporate HR, and by interrogators. The line between psychometrics and mind hacking is mostly about consent.
psychometrics.hooks: the screener who runs Firewall's contamination protocols; the corporate psychometrician who quit over what they were asked to measure; the consultant who can tell you whether your fork came back wrong.

martian-techno.name: Martian Techno
martian-techno.setting: Post-Fall Martian subculture — the music, fashion, slang, and street life of Valles-New Shanghai and the lesser domes, plus the nomad cultures of the surface. The Barsoomian political edge runs through a lot of it. Techno here is a loose stand-in for the whole post-Fall Martian street aesthetic, where Consortium hypercapital, autonomist sympathies, and old Earth diasporas collide.
martian-techno.hooks: the Martian club kid who knows every venue; the underground promoter with autonomist ties; the journalist who covers the scene because everything that matters on Mars eventually shows up in it.

night-clubs.name: Night Clubs
night-clubs.setting: Habitat nightlife — venues, scenes, door politics, drug scenes, who plays where, who runs which room. In EP2 a club can be VR-only, simulspace, full-spectrum sensory, or a converted cargo bay; the social rules vary wildly by polity. Inner system clubs lean curated and corporate; outer system clubs are anarchic and weird. Universally a place where information moves.
night-clubs.hooks: the doorperson who knows every face in the local scene; the promoter who has run venues in three habitats; the off-duty operator who treats clubs as the best intel-collection environment in any habitat.

pop-culture.name: Pop Culture
pop-culture.setting: The mass media of transhumanity — XP series, AR shows, music codelines, celebrity feeds, simulspace fandoms, AGI-made art, uplift creators going viral. Different polities consume differently: Lunar fashion houses set the white-collar style, Martian streamers dominate XP, Titanian art-collectives produce most of what the autonomists watch. Pop culture is also how memes propagate.
pop-culture.hooks: the fan whose collection is encyclopedic; the cultural critic with cross-polity reach; the producer who has worked enough scenes to see how they all connect.

celebrity-gossip.name: Celebrity Gossip
celebrity-gossip.setting: Knowing who is sleeping with whom, which celebrity died and got resleeved into a new face, which Lunar designer is feuding with which Martian streamer, which hypercorp exec just lost their fork in a divorce. In an immortal society where you can resleeve into anyone you like, celebrity gossip touches identity, IP rights, and reputation in tangled ways.
celebrity-gossip.hooks: the gossip columnist with sources in every habitat; the ex-celebrity assistant who knows the real story; the rep-broker who reads gossip as market data.

current-events.name: Current Events
current-events.setting: The news cycle of transhumanity — Consortium press releases, autonomist counter-news, hypercorp feuds, gatecrashing reports, Mercurial rights actions, the latest exsurgent scare, fresh political maneuvers in the Tharsis League. Spread thin across polities and feeds; nobody sees the same news, which is half the problem.
current-events.hooks: the news junkie who reads across faction lines; the political analyst with strong opinions; the freelance journalist trying to make a living telling the truth.

conspiracies.name: Conspiracies
conspiracies.setting: Theories about what really happened during the Fall, who is really behind Project Ozma, what the Factors actually want, whether the TITANs really left, who runs Pax Familae, what Firewall is hiding. In Eclipse Phase, a lot of the conspiracy theories are true — and a lot of the true ones are even worse than the rumors. Knowing the landscape of conspiracy lore means knowing which threads are bait and which lead somewhere lethal.
conspiracies.hooks: the conspiracy hobbyist who accidentally got too close; the ex-spook who confirms three theories and denies the worst one; the Firewall asset who plants disinformation to bury the truth.

serial-killers.name: Serial Killers
serial-killers.setting: In a society where death is reversible, serial killing has mutated — sleeve-killing for the thrill, ego-snuff via psychosurgery, repeated murder of the same victim across multiple resleeves, Nine Lives-style ritual cruelty. Knowledge of serial killers means knowing the famous cases, the patterns investigators look for, and the new kinds of killer that only make sense in a post-Fall body economy.
serial-killers.hooks: the criminologist who specializes in post-Fall murder patterns; the survivor who has been killed before and remembers parts of it; the ex-cop who hunts the worst offenders off the record.

religion.name: Religion
religion.setting: Faith after the Fall — surviving traditions (Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism, Mormonism, pagan paths) adapting to resleeving, AGI souls, uplift congregants, simulspace pilgrimages. Plus the new post-Fall religions, TITAN-worshipping cults, exhuman millennialism, and the unsettling religions practiced on certain exoplanet colonies. Knowing religion in EP2 is knowing how billions of transhumans make meaning under conditions that used to be theological impossibilities.
religion.hooks: the theology scholar with cross-tradition reach; the chaplain who has counseled re-instantiated infugees; the cult investigator who knows which sects are dangerous and which are just sad.

mathematics.name: Mathematics
mathematics.setting: Abstract reasoning, calculation, proof. In EP2 the discipline underpins cryptography, physics, programming, and the deep work of AGI design. Skill in mathematics is a quiet credential that opens technical doors across factions.
mathematics.hooks: the academic mathematician whose papers get cited in unexpected fields.

biology.name: Biology
biology.setting: The science of living systems — genetics, biochemistry, ecology, physiology. In EP2 the field has expanded to include alien biology and exoplanet ecologies sampled through the gates.
biology.hooks: the biologist who has worked off-world enough to question Earth-centric textbooks.

chemistry.name: Chemistry
chemistry.setting: The science of substances and their reactions. In EP2 it sits adjacent to nanofabrication, drug synthesis, biochem, and material science for hostile environments.
chemistry.hooks: the chemist who can identify a compound by feel; the synthesist who quietly cooks for autonomist clinics.

physics.name: Physics
physics.setting: The fundamental science of matter, energy, motion. In EP2 it includes the open mysteries of pandora gates, antimatter containment, fusion drive engineering, and the wormhole physics nobody has fully solved.
physics.hooks: the theoretician obsessed with the gates; the propulsion engineer who has watched too many drive tests go wrong.

geology.name: Geology
geology.setting: The science of rock, planetary surfaces, and what lies beneath them. In EP2 geology covers Mars, Luna, asteroid mining surveys, planetary habitat construction, and exoplanet first-in geology reports.
geology.hooks: the field geologist who has surveyed three exoplanets; the asteroid prospector who reads rock the way others read text.

sociology.name: Sociology
sociology.setting: The study of transhuman societies — habitat cultures, factional dynamics, post-Fall identity formation, the sociology of forks and mercurials and immortal populations. A field reinvented under post-scarcity, post-mortality conditions.
sociology.hooks: the sociologist whose models actually predict habitat unrest; the field researcher embedded in a fringe community.

psychology.name: Psychology
psychology.setting: The science of mind and behavior. In EP2 psychology grapples with mass post-Fall trauma, resleeving disorders, fork-merge stress, infomorph isolation, and the unique pressures of being transhuman.
psychology.hooks: the therapist who specializes in re-instantiated infugees; the researcher mapping new disorders unique to the post-Fall age.

music.name: Music
music.setting: Composition, performance, criticism. In EP2 music spans Lunar pop, Martian techno, autonomist noise, simulspace orchestras, and AGI-composed pieces that no human played. A reputation skill in scenes where creative output drives social standing.
music.hooks: the musician whose work crosses polity lines.

dance.name: Dance
dance.setting: Performance and movement art across morphs and gravities. EP2 dance includes microgravity ballet, exotic-morph choreography, simulspace forms impossible in physical space.
dance.hooks: the dancer who has performed in every gravity regime in the system.

sculpture.name: Sculpture
sculpture.setting: Three-dimensional art — traditional materials, nanofab assemblies, bio-sculpted living forms (MeatHab is the most famous), simulspace volumetric works. In EP2 the line between sculpture, morph design, and habitat architecture blurs.
sculpture.hooks: the sculptor who works in nanofab; the bio-artist whose pieces grow.

fine-art.name: Fine Art
fine-art.setting: Painting, drawing, criticism, appraisal. In EP2 fine art includes AR and VR-native forms, AGI-generated pieces (including from the **!** codeline), and the surviving canon of pre-Fall Earth art preserved through the Fall as cultural treasure.
fine-art.hooks: the appraiser who can spot a forgery in any medium; the critic with cross-polity reach.

sports.name: Sports
sports.setting: Competitive games and athletics — including microgravity sports, cross-morph competitions, simulspace e-sports, hard-vacuum events, and the surviving Earth traditions adapted to off-world play. A reputation-rich field in many habitats.
sports.hooks: the ex-pro athlete in a new morph; the sports journalist with system-wide reach.

education.name: Education
education.setting: The institutions and practices of teaching — academy systems, apprenticeships, simulspace classrooms, skillware training, AGI tutors. Differs enormously by polity: Consortium tracks heavily by hypercorp affiliation, autonomists prefer collective and self-directed models.
education.hooks: the educator who has worked under three polities and has opinions; the curriculum designer trying to teach the post-Fall generation.

journalism.name: Journalism
journalism.setting: Reporting, investigation, narrative framing. In EP2 journalism overlaps with memetics — every faction runs media, and the line between news and propaganda is contested. XP-driven journalism is increasingly common; so is journalist disappearance.
journalism.hooks: the investigative reporter with too many enemies; the XP journalist who walks into the story.

law.name: Law
law.setting: Polity-specific legal codes — Consortium IP law, LLA Council rulings, Titanian micro-democratic statutes, Jovian Republic security law, the anarchist absence of law as a legal stance in itself. Cross-polity work means knowing many overlapping and sometimes incompatible systems.
law.hooks: the cross-polity lawyer who specializes in extradition; the ex-prosecutor who saw the system from the inside.

accounting.name: Accounting
accounting.setting: Financial recordkeeping and analysis — for hypercorp ledgers, cartel laundering, anarchist mutual-aid economies, Titanian reputation economies. EP2 accounting frequently doubles as forensic work since money trails reveal politics.
accounting.hooks: the forensic accountant who follows the rep flows; the ex-corporate auditor with leaked files.

economics.name: Economics
economics.setting: The science of resource allocation. In EP2 economics covers post-scarcity rep economies, hypercapitalism, transitional gift economies, indenture markets, and the open question of what value means when nanofabrication can print almost anything.
economics.hooks: the economist who actually understands rep markets; the autonomist theorist arguing the inner system is the anomaly.

stock-market.name: Stock Market
stock-market.setting: The hypercorp equity and futures markets — Consortium exchanges, Extropian shanzhai-friendly markets, the prediction markets that double as informal political intelligence. Insider trading is universal; only some of it is prosecuted.
stock-market.hooks: the trader who reads political winds in pricing; the ex-analyst who lost their fork in a margin call.

drugs.name: Drugs
drugs.setting: Pharmacology in a society where bodies are interchangeable — recreational nanodrugs, narcoalgorithms (drugs that run as code on cyberbrains), nootropics, custom-tailored substances, the persistent legal mess of cross-polity drug laws. Adjacent to the dark XP scene and the black market broadly.
drugs.hooks: the pharmacologist who works clean and underground; the user who has tried everything and lived; the cartel chemist trying to retire.

instruction.name: Instruction
instruction.setting: The professional practice of teaching specific skills — combat training, technical instruction, simulspace coaching, apprentice mentorship. Distinct from academic education: instruction is hands-on transfer of capability.
instruction.hooks: the veteran trainer who has taught a generation; the instructor who specializes in skillware-augmented learning.

administration.name: Administration
administration.setting: The professional work of running organizations — habitat bureaucracy, hypercorp office politics, cartel logistics, autonomist collective coordination. Procedure knowledge, who reports to who, how to grease which wheel.
administration.hooks: the ex-corporate administrator who knows where the keys are kept; the collective coordinator who has actually made a horizontal organization work.

surveying.name: Surveying
surveying.setting: Mapping and resource assessment — habitat interiors, asteroid bodies, exoplanet first-in zones, planetary surfaces. Heavy use of drones and remote sensors; the surveyor's expertise is what to look for and what the readings mean.
surveying.hooks: the surveyor who has charted exoplanet sites for the gatecrashing corps.

mining.name: Mining
