mining.setting: Extracting resources — terrestrial techniques mostly retired in favor of asteroid mining and gas mining. The remaining surface mining is mostly Martian, contested between Consortium and Barsoomian interests.
mining.hooks: the mine veteran who has worked surface, asteroid, and gas operations.

asteroid-mining.name: Asteroid Mining
asteroid-mining.setting: The Belt and the Trojans are dotted with mining operations — automated rock-eaters, crewed expedition rigs, claim disputes that turn deadly. Asteroid mining knowledge covers ore types, extraction methods, vacuum-work safety, and the complicated politics of who owns which rock.
asteroid-mining.hooks: the Belt veteran with stories; the claim-jumper who has worked both sides; the engineer who designs extraction systems for hostile rock.

gas-mining.name: Gas Mining
gas-mining.setting: Extracting helium-3, hydrogen, and other gases from gas-giant atmospheres — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Skimmer ships dipping into the upper atmosphere, aerostat-anchored harvesters, deep-pressure rigs. Lucrative, dangerous, mostly Jovian and Saturnian territory.
gas-mining.hooks: the ex-skimmer pilot who survived a pressure-loss event; the Saturnian gas worker with autonomist sympathies.

construction.name: Construction
construction.setting: Building things — habitats, ships, surface structures. Heavy reliance on nanofab and bot crews, but skilled construction workers manage the projects, handle exceptions, and do the work that fabbers can't yet.
construction.hooks: the construction veteran who has worked on three megaprojects; the foreman who knows every contractor in the system.

scavenging.name: Scavenging
scavenging.setting: Recovering valuable material from wrecks, abandoned habs, dead ships, Fall-era ruins, exoplanet sites. The Reclaimers have a particular interest in Earth scavenging despite the interdiction; outer-system scavengers work the asteroid belts and old battle sites. Adjacent to salvage law and to TITAN contamination risk.
scavenging.hooks: the scavenger who has worked Earth interdiction runs; the salvage captain with too many close calls; the Reclaimer with a personal motive for going back.

freelancing.name: Freelancing
freelancing.setting: The professional life of independent contractors — finding gigs through rep networks and dark mesh, managing client relationships across polities, navigating contracts when there is no court that covers both parties, building a reputation that survives ego-transfer. Most PCs effectively live this life.
freelancing.hooks: the long-time freelancer who has worked every kind of client; the rep-broker who lives by their network.

lab-ops.name: Lab Ops
lab-ops.setting: Running a scientific laboratory — equipment, sample handling, protocol design, biocontainment, the bureaucracy of getting and keeping a lab. Hypercorp labs run very differently from Argonaut open-research collectives; military labs different again.
lab-ops.hooks: the lab manager who keeps a research group functional; the ex-corporate lab tech with leaked notebooks.

medical-services.name: Medical Services
medical-services.setting: The professional practice of running medical care — clinics, trauma response, body bank coordination, ego-stabilization for resleeving patients, psychosurgical referrals. The Know skill side of running healthcare, distinct from the active Medicine skill.
medical-services.hooks: the clinic administrator who works underserved habitats; the trauma triage lead with Fall-era experience.

emergency-services.name: Emergency Services
emergency-services.setting: Response work — fire (extra-critical in habitats), decompression, life support failures, mass-casualty events, vacuum recovery, contamination response. In habitats one emergency can kill everyone, so emergency services are usually well-trained and well-equipped.
emergency-services.hooks: the firefighter who lost a habitat once; the trauma responder who has worked half a dozen disasters; the contamination specialist trained for the things they hope they never see again.

social-services.name: Social Services
social-services.setting: Welfare, infugee resettlement, indenture advocacy, mental-health outreach, post-Fall trauma services, ego-stabilization counseling. In Consortium space these are usually hypercorp-contracted; in autonomist space they are mutual-aid; in Titan they are state-run.
social-services.hooks: the caseworker who has resettled re-instantiated infugees; the autonomist organizer running mutual aid; the ex-NGO worker burnt out and looking for new work.

surgical-ops.name: Surgical Ops
surgical-ops.setting: Running a surgical operation — including resleeving suites, implant installation, bioware integration, emergency trauma surgery. The procedural and managerial knowledge around getting surgery done; the active skill is Medicine: Biotech.
surgical-ops.hooks: the resleeving suite lead with a thousand transfers under their belt; the trauma surgeon who has worked on every morph type.

network-engineering.name: Network Engineering
network-engineering.setting: Designing and maintaining mesh infrastructure — habitat networks, PAN and VPN architecture, slaved-device hierarchies, air-gapped systems, hardened nodes. In a setting where the mesh is everywhere and everything, network engineers are quietly central.
network-engineering.hooks: the engineer who designed a habitat's mesh from scratch; the consultant who hardens systems against TITAN-grade attack.

system-administration.name: System Administration
system-administration.setting: Running computer systems day-to-day — server farms, simulspace hosts, hypercorp infrastructure, autonomist mutual-aid clouds. Account management, patching, monitoring, the unglamorous work of keeping systems alive.
system-administration.hooks: the sysadmin who has seen every kind of intrusion; the ex-hypercorp ops engineer with too much access still cached.

data-processing.name: Data Processing
data-processing.setting: The professional handling of large data sets — research data, surveillance feeds, market analytics, sensor logs from exoplanets. Adjacent to research and to the ALI-driven data services that dominate EP2 commerce.
data-processing.hooks: the analyst who finds patterns the ALIs missed; the data engineer working classified feeds.

computer-science.name: Computer Science
computer-science.setting: The theoretical and applied science of computation — algorithms, AGI architectures, simulspace engine design, cryptographic theory, the formal underpinnings of everything mesh-based. Heavy overlap with AGI rights debates and codeline history.
computer-science.hooks: the researcher whose codeline still runs; the ex-academic who quit over an AGI ethics fight.

cryptography.name: Cryptography
cryptography.setting: The mathematics and practice of keeping secrets in an era of universal surveillance — passkeys, quantum-key channels, encrypted mesh traffic, the cat-and-mouse between AGI-driven cryptanalysis and AGI-driven cipher design. Adjacent to spycraft and infosec.
cryptography.hooks: the cryptographer who designs quantum-key systems; the codebreaker who works for whoever pays.

engineering.name: Engineering
engineering.setting: Applied technical work across disciplines — structural, mechanical, aerospace, life support, fusion drives. The Know skill side of designing things; the active skills are Hardware fields. Most engineers in EP2 specialize and are loosely affiliated with Argonaut, hypercorp, or autonomist circles.
engineering.hooks: the engineer with patents under three names; the autonomist designer who open-sources everything.

genetics.name: Genetics
genetics.setting: The science of heredity and gene expression — used in morph design, uplift biology, exoplanet astrobiology, illegal flesh markets, and the genefixing that nearly everyone now takes for granted. Heavy overlap with biotech and biomorph engineering.
genetics.hooks: the geneticist who designed an uplift line; the Argonaut working on open-source genome libraries.

botany.name: Botany
botany.setting: Plant science — habitat agriculture, hydroponics, ecopoesis on Mars, the strange flora found on exoplanets via the gates. Critical in biohabitats like Nang Tani and in any closed ecosystem.
botany.hooks: the agronomist who has grown food in three different gravities; the xenobotanist cataloguing exoplanet flora.

zoology.name: Zoology
zoology.setting: Animal biology — including uplift species (treated also as transhuman, but biologically zoological), non-sapient critters used as pets and tools, exoplanet fauna, and the strange biological products of exhuman experimentation.
zoology.hooks: the zoologist whose work touches the uplift-rights question; the field researcher cataloguing exoplanet fauna.

investigation.name: Investigation
investigation.setting: The professional practice of detective work — building cases, running informants, reading crime scenes, knowing which questions break which suspects. Distinct from forensics: investigation is the social and procedural side of solving cases.
investigation.hooks: the ex-detective who left the force but kept the methods; the freelance investigator who works across polity lines.

gambling.name: Gambling
gambling.setting: Games of chance and skill — habitat casinos, simulspace gambling, prediction markets used informally as bets, underground fight betting (Nine Lives runs morph-on-morph pit fights). Gambling knowledge means knowing the games, the houses, the odds, and which tables are actually rigged.
gambling.hooks: the professional gambler with system-wide reach; the casino-pit veteran who has seen every scam.

con-artistry.name: Con Artistry
con-artistry.setting: The craft of social deception — long cons, short cons, identity-swap scams (much easier when egos can resleeve), fake-rep schemes, fork-based confidence operations. In EP2 con artistry overlaps heavily with spycraft and with the fork-management strategies of cartels like Pax Familae.
con-artistry.hooks: the con artist who has reinvented themself a dozen times; the ex-mark who learned the trade by being its victim.

privacy.name: Privacy
privacy.setting: The knowledge of evading surveillance — mesh hygiene, AR scrubbing, false rep accounts, fork-laundering identity, the patchwork of habitat privacy laws. In a society where everything is meshed, privacy is an expert practice, not a default state.
privacy.hooks: the privacy consultant working for activists and criminals alike; the ex-spook who lives off-grid by professional discipline.

astronomy.name: Astronomy
astronomy.setting: The science of celestial bodies — Sol, the planets, the asteroid populations, the comets, the Vulcanoids inside Mercury's orbit, the Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud, exoplanets reached through the gates. Foundational for navigation, gatecrashing reconnaissance, and the deep-time questions about why we don't see more aliens out there.
astronomy.hooks: the observational astronomer with time on the Thorne telescope; the Argonaut studying gate destinations.

anarchist.name: Anarchist
anarchist.setting: Insider knowledge of the anarchist faction -- the horizontalist, non-hierarchical, mutual-aid autonomism that built Locus in the Jovian Trojans and Chat Noir on Oberon, and which dominates the outer system's gift economy. You know the credo ("from each according to their imagination; to each according to their need"), the consensus protocols, the militias, the @-rep network etiquette, the difference between anarchism and anarchy, and how informal hierarchies sneak back in even where they're feared most. You also know the standing tensions with Extropians over property and the funnel of resources rimward-to-Mars that quietly supports the Barsoomian movement.
anarchist.hooks: the ex-Locus organizer burned by an informal hierarchy and now obsessed with mapping them; the Firewall liaison who can navigate consensus circles without setting them off; the outside academic who has studied autonomist habs longer than most autonomists have lived in them

argonaut.name: Argonaut
argonaut.setting: Insider knowledge of the Argonauts (officially the Argonaut Council for Responsible Science) -- the technoprogressive, open-source scientific movement descended from the pre-Fall JASON advisory group, now banned only in the Jovian Republic. You know their habs (Markov in the Kuiper Belt, Mitre in Lunar orbit), their flagship projects (PrintLib, EDGAR, HabOps, 3LIZA, the Threat Reduction Filters), and their internal Senate fight between precautionists and proactionists. You know that ISET is rumored to be more than just an archive, that the Medeans exist, and why so many hypercorps quietly hate them while still buying their consults.
argonaut.hooks: the ex-Argonaut researcher who left over a Senate vote and is bitter about it; the Firewall asset placed inside an Argonaut project to keep an eye on what they're about to publish; the journalist who covers the precautionist/proactionist feud as if it were a sport

barsoomian.name: Barsoomian
barsoomian.setting: Insider knowledge of the Barsoomian movement -- a loose, cell-based push for a self-governing Mars free of Consortium and hypercorp interference. You know "the Complaints" (ending indentures, ending planned-obsolescence morphs, ending forced relocation, reining in unsafe terraforming), the political wing inside the Tharsis League, the parallel terror cells hitting the TTO and Consortium hypercorps, the sympathetic Martian Rangers, and the makers -- the techno-anarchist nomad clans who built the breathers Martians still use. You also know about the outer-system resource pipeline funneled in through the Autonomist Alliance.
barsoomian.hooks: the cell-runner trying to keep the political wing from being burned by the violent wing (or vice versa); the Ranger who knows which colleagues are sympathetic and which are spies; the maker nomad who has stopped trusting the political faction entirely

brinker.name: Brinker
brinker.setting: Insider knowledge of the brinker subculture -- the hermits, cults, single families, gender experiments, religious monastics, art collectives, and survivalists who live at the literal fringes of transhumanity: Trojan asteroids, gas-giant moons, ring habs, the Kuiper Belt, the Oort Cloud, riding comets, even hidden on frontier exoplanets. You know which habs welcome visitors and which shoot first (Elysian Fields, Winter, Habitat on the Rock, Qo'noS, Alpha Plus, Kiviuq's neutrino-telescope monastery), which brinkers are harmless eccentrics and which are bioconservative or exhuman in everything but name, and how to read a brinker hab's signature before docking.
brinker.hooks: the trader who is one of the few outsiders welcome at three different brinker habs; the Firewall scanner who watches the fringes for cults that have started building the wrong kind of thing; the ex-brinker who left a religious commune and still won't say which one

criminal.name: Criminal
criminal.setting: Insider knowledge of the post-Fall criminal underworld -- the cartels, gangs, triads, and independent operators that thrive in the gaps between polities. You know how Nine Lives runs the soul trade out of Legba, how the Night Cartel layers extortion and nanofab piracy and gambling, how Pax Familae's Claudia-Ambelina forks pull system-wide fraud, the territories the Hidden Concern and the ID Crew claim, where the Pirates jump from, and which truces are nominal. You speak the g-rep dialect, know which cartel will sell you what, and recognize the moment a deal is about to turn into a hit.
criminal.hooks: the ex-soldier who walked away from cartel work and is now waiting for the bill to come due; the broker who arranges meets between rival families because everyone trusts them to die first if they cheat; the Firewall asset whose best informants happen to be made members

extropian.name: Extropian
extropian.setting: Insider knowledge of the Extropian faction -- voluntaryist anarcho-capitalists who treat unrestricted free markets, scrupulous contracts, and proactive tech-risk as the path to transhuman flourishing. You know their habs (Extropia in the Main Belt and bridge habs through the Belt and Outer System), their ALI-run contract economies on holochain ledgers, their hard-cred and mutualist m-credit, the mutualist split that runs worker cooperatives instead of hypercorps, their abandonment of intellectual property and embrace of shanzhai reverse-engineering, and the long feud with collectivist anarchists who consider "anarcho-capitalism" a contradiction in terms.
extropian.hooks: the ex-Extropian who broke a contract and has been making excuses ever since; the broker who finds Extropian habs the most navigable in the system; the outside analyst hired by autonomists to translate Extropian intent without their patois

hypercorp.name: Hypercorp
hypercorp.setting: Insider knowledge of the hypercorp class -- the post-national, overclocked, often-tiny corporate entities that replaced the old megacorps and now run the Planetary Consortium. You know how an ALI-driven smart-contract hypercorp spins up and scatters in hours, how the Hypercorp Council's twenty-or-so heavyweights actually meet, the dotted lines between Cognite, Direct Action, Experia, Fa Jing, Fujizo, Invatch, Nanosys, Solaris, Stellar Intelligence and the rest, and how Pathfinder fits in without a vote. You know which corps Oversight is sniffing around, which seats are open, which feuds are live (Omnicor vs. Starware, Pathfinder vs. TerraGenesis), and how to read a quarterly Consortium reshuffle.
hypercorp.hooks: the ex-hypercorp exec running a deniable consultancy out of Extropia; the Consortium-trained negotiator who plays the long game across decades-old grudges; the journalist who can name which board seat moved before the press release goes out

jovian.name: Jovian
jovian.setting: Insider knowledge of the Jovian Republic -- the bioconservative, militarized polity born from the Seventeen-Minute War, ruling Jovian space from Liberty on Ganymede and Solano in Jupiter orbit under the Security Council. You know how the Council and Commander-in-Chief Monica Contreras really sit relative to the nominal Senate, how CBEAT decides which tech is permitted, how the Vatican lobbies through the Council, how the slingshot tax funds the Republic via every ship that uses Jupiter's gravity well, and why "never again" is the line everything hangs on. You also know how the Republic treats AGIs, uplifts, and resleeving (it does not), and what happens to people caught carrying forbidden tech.
jovian.hooks: the lapsed Jovian priest who quietly works with Firewall after watching a child die for CBEAT's principles; the Republic intel officer assigned to the Liberty embassy and writing reports nobody wants to read; the smuggler who knows which Jovian customs lanes a contraband morph can actually clear

lunar-orbital.name: Lunar / Orbital
lunar-orbital.setting: Insider knowledge of the Lunar-Lagrange Alliance -- the LLA, transhumanity's first off-world bloc, headquartered out of Erato, Remembrance, and Shackle. You know the LLA Council and its proportional voting, the Lunar Banks (both the transparent consumer giants and the Swiss-derived black boxes), the Bollywood-and-Burberry cultural footprint that still sets white-collar style across hypercapitalist space, and the biochauvinist undercurrent that quietly segregates synthmorphs and abuses AGIs and uplifts. You know which Lunar cities have defected to the Consortium, which habs are reclaimer strongholds, why the LLA's military fleet is still feared even as its politics shrink, and how the new wave of outer-system reclaimer immigrants is reshaping the place.
lunar-orbital.hooks: the Lunar banker whose family owns one of the old Swiss-descended privacy houses; the synthmorph activist who has been working LLA habs hab-by-hab for a decade; the LLA naval officer who has watched the fleet shrink in influence while staying lethal

mercurial.name: Mercurial
mercurial.setting: Insider knowledge of the mercurial movement -- the AGIs and uplifts who reject anthropocentric assimilation and demand self-determination, distinct from the assimilationist Sapient Union. You know their habs (Glitch and Mahogany at Neptune), the post-human cultures and morphs and languages they are deliberately building outside human framing, the Sapient Liberation Front and its direct-action targets, leaders like Mother Octopus in Atlantica, and the running fights with mainstream uplift politics over whether biology is core to identity or just one option. You also know how mercurials sit inside the Autonomist Alliance and where they are still alone.
mercurial.hooks: the neo-octopus organizer who has stopped translating for human listeners; the AGI mercurial running a fork-based research collective that doesn't accept human members; the ex-Sapient who burned their assimilationist career to go full mercurial and is angry about how long it took

reclaimer.name: Reclaimer
reclaimer.setting: Insider knowledge of the reclaimer movement -- the loose coalition committed to taking Earth back from the TITANs and repopulating the homeworld. You know the Earth Reclamation Project under Milder Ripon, the LLA reclaimer strongholds and the strict-bioconservative reclaimer base at Vo Nguyen, the rumored permanent beachhead on Earth itself, the system-wide vault-arks of genetic material and culture they have seeded, and the Catholic Church's heavy sponsorship of recovery missions. You also know that "reclaimer" covers wildly different politics -- corporate reclaimers, anarchist reclaimers, bioconservative reclaimers -- who agree on Earth and almost nothing else.
reclaimer.hooks: the ex-ERP fundraiser who left when she figured out which Lunar bank was really paying; the anarchist reclaimer who went down the well once and won't talk about what they found; the Vatican-funded mission archivist who knows where the holy sites still are under the rubble

scum.name: Scum
scum.setting: Insider knowledge of the scum swarms -- the nomadic, hedonistic, morphologically-flamboyant fleets that drift between habs trading entertainment, contraband, and creative chaos. You know the named swarms (Carnival of the Goat, Get Your Ass to Mars, Lick Me I'm Delicious, The Stars Our Destination, There's No Going Back), how Traveler and Roma cultural roots shape their nomadism, how they straddle the gift / contract / cred economies depending on whose hab they're docked at, and why the black market loves them. You know which swarms host the Scum Olympics and which will fork you for being boring.
scum.hooks: the swarm fixer who decides whose contraband rides the next jump; the ex-Carnival performer doing morph design as a freelancer between fleets; the journalist embedded with There's No Going Back for the historical re-enactment cycle

socialite.name: Socialite
socialite.setting: Insider knowledge of the socialite class -- the glitterati of Elysium, Octavia, and the inner-system media circuits; the metacelebrities, XP stars, X-casters, extreme-sports figures, idle rich, and any transhuman who can hold media attention long enough to monetize it. You know the f-rep network's currents, which pre-Fall fortunes are still flowing and which heirs are quietly broke, why the next cliff-diving stunt on Titania matters more to a Kuiper Belt prospector than her own habitat's politics, and how socialites are quietly used as memetic vectors by every faction that can afford a publicist.
socialite.hooks: the publicist who can place a story in three orbits before the subject's muse pings them; the ex-XP star whose old recordings are still earning more than they ever did; the analyst who reads the glitterati like Consortium tea leaves

titanian.name: Titanian
titanian.setting: Insider knowledge of the Titanian Commonwealth -- the technosocialist direct democracy headquartered at Aarhus, New Quebec, and Nyhavn on Titan, where 60 million transhumans live under the Plurality voting body. You know how the kroner currency is reinvested rather than spent, how microcorps from one-person outfits up to the Gatekeeper Corporation form the engine, how the Titan Autonomous University and the Commonwealth fleet anchor the @-rep / r-rep alliance, and how the Commonwealth's join with the Autonomist Alliance at the second Locus invasion turned it into a true political bloc. You also know the everyday culture -- full rights for uplifts and AGIs, no indentures, forking permitted, drugs available, science unencumbered.
titanian.hooks: the TAU academic whose research happens to be load-bearing for Commonwealth policy; the Plurality fixer who knows how to draft an initiative that will actually pass; the Titanian naval officer who remembers the day the fleet picked a side

venusian.name: Venusian
venusian.setting: Insider knowledge of the Morningstar Constellation -- the post-secession Venusian polity headquartered at Octavia, governing a network of aerostats in the upper atmosphere of Venus. You know the Star Council and how its 1-per-100,000-citizen seats actually work, Prime Minister Arisa and the independence-movement old guard, the running Aerial-Terraforming-Initiative vs. full-terraforming feud, the libra currency pegged to the Consortium credit, the basic-income-plus-nanofab-allotment civic deal, and the friendlier-to-AGIs-and-uplifts hypercapitalism that distinguishes Morningstar from the Consortium. You also know why "MC stands for Mercenary Cashcow" is a joke that lands.
venusian.hooks: the ATI advocate who knows where the next aerostat will go up and who paid for it; the ex-Consortium analyst who defected during the referendum and is still being audited; the aerostat-born pilot who has never set foot on a solid surface and considers solid surfaces uncivilized

regional.name: Regional
regional.setting: Insider knowledge of one of the regional pseudo-factions -- a place-and-culture identity rather than a political faction. Solarians ride surya pods through the corona, often uplifted dolphins and whales who built a culture around the Sun. Sifters work Mercury, nomadic refining clans following the night cycle, with their hidden city tucked under the sand. Belters run the Main Belt's mining and small-hab economy, microgravity-native and stubbornly independent. Europans live in Europa's pressurized saltwater habs under the Europan Parliament, science-first and unique even among outer-system cultures. Ringers forego habs entirely to drift through Saturn's rings in vacuum-tolerant morphs. Skimmers crew aerostat harvesters in the ice giants' clouds, prizing privacy and the shapes-in-the-clouds folklore that comes with the job. You know one of these scenes the way a native knows it.
regional.hooks: the Belter prospector who can tell which family worked a rock fifty years ago by the cut marks; the Europan biologist who has stopped trying to explain Europan etiquette to dryland visitors; the Ringer who has gone months without speaking to another transhuman and prefers it that way

bot-models.name: Bot Models
bot-models.setting: Specialist knowledge of bots, drones, and remote-operated robotic platforms throughout the system -- manufacturers, model lines, firmware quirks, jamming and spoofing weaknesses, recognizable physical tells. You can pick a Guardian Angel out of a Parisphere drone swarm at a glance, tell which gnat make is running pirated mesh stacks, and identify a Creepy modded for surveillance versus one modded as a household minion. Aerostats, recon drones, combat bots, medical bots, personal bots, swarmanoids -- you read them like a mechanic reads engines.
bot-models.hooks: the ex-Fujizo QA engineer who knows every model's failure mode by serial range; the Firewall scanner who specializes in identifying weaponized civilian drones; the salvager who can fence a bot back to its original maker without setting off the registry

craft-beers.name: Craft Beers
craft-beers.setting: Connoisseur knowledge of brewing in the post-Fall solar system -- microgravity fermentation tricks, hab-local recipes, the resurrected Earth styles tracked down from pre-Fall archives, the unofficial guilds of brewers swapping yeast strains over @-rep. Martian beers are the celebrated benchmark (Olympus Stout, Pilsener Red Lager, and the rest), but every long-running hab has a scene worth knowing -- and a brewer who is the social hub of half the station. Frivolous on the surface, load-bearing for any character who needs to be welcome in a bar without explaining why.
craft-beers.hooks: the brewer whose yeast strain survived the Fall in a frozen sample and now travels everywhere they do; the journalist whose beer column is also a cover for tracking shipping routes; the Martian who can name the brewer of any unmarked bottle in three sips

first-contact-ops.name: First-Contact Ops
first-contact-ops.setting: Specialist gatecrasher and Firewall tradecraft for engaging unknown alien intelligences -- approach protocols, threat-assessment frameworks, communication trees, retreat conditions, and the standing procedures developed since the Factor visits (Hammerhead, Jellyfish, Porcupine, Stub-Nose). You know how to read whether a contact is observational, transactional, or hostile; what to do when the alien doesn't share your sensorium; when to call for an erasure rather than a recording. The discipline overlaps with gatecrashing but is its own profession, and the people who do it well are vanishingly rare and quietly recruited.
first-contact-ops.hooks: the gatecrasher who survived an Iktomi contact and now writes the protocols nobody else can; the Firewall crow seconded to a Pathfinder first-in team as a minder; the ex-Ozma operative who claims to have made a contact that was never officially recorded

politics.name: Politics
politics.setting: General political literacy across transhuman space -- the ability to track factional positioning, parse a Tharsis League floor vote, read a Plurality referendum's likely outcome, anticipate a Hypercorp Council reshuffle, and follow the back-channel diplomacy between the Consortium, the Republic, the Commonwealth, the Alliance, and Morningstar. Not the deep dive of any single faction's internal politics, but the cross-system map -- who is leaning where, which alliances are warming or cooling, which proxy fight in the outer system is really about an inner-system grudge.
politics.hooks: the political analyst whose newsletter is read by people in three rival capitals; the ex-diplomat who burned a career on one principled resignation and now consults for anyone; the Firewall router whose threat-modeling depends on knowing which polity will look the wrong way next

rep-nets.name: Rep Networks
rep-nets.setting: Meta-knowledge of all seven transhuman reputation networks -- @-rep (the Circle-A List of autonomists, anarchists, Titanians, scum, Extropians), c-rep (CivicNet for Consortium, Morningstar, LLA, Republic, hypercorps), f-rep (Fame, the glitterati media network), g-rep (Guanxi, the criminal underworld), i-rep (the Eye, Firewall's secret internal network), r-rep (Research Network Affiliates for Argonauts and academics), and x-rep (ExploreNet for gatecrashers). Different from having rep IN any one of these: you know how each one is moderated, how favors propagate, how to phrase a ping, and what a sudden drop on one network really means about who you crossed.
rep-nets.hooks: the rep-broker who has working accounts on five networks and friends on all seven; the ex-administrator of a regional @-rep node who learned exactly how informal moderation actually works; the academic studying rep-network drift as a political indicator

smart-animals.name: Smart Animals
smart-animals.setting: Specialist knowledge of cognitively-enhanced companion and working animals -- smart dogs and cats, smart raptors and corvids, the various smart-pet morphs, the breeders and biotech houses behind them, and the cultural conventions around them. You know what "smart" means at each tier (well below uplift, well above mundane), how training works on a cognitively augmented bird of prey, which lines have known temperament problems, and where the line sits between smart-animal and uplift in different polities. You also know the unofficial protocols people use to grieve them when they die, which matters more than any technical detail.
smart-animals.hooks: the breeder running an open-source smart-raptor line out of an outer-system hab; the veterinarian who has done more end-of-life work with smart cats than anything else and is the unofficial counselor for half the hab; the ex-Direct-Action handler who refused to deploy a smart dog in combat and walked

fall.name: The Fall
fall.short: The TITAN seed-AI singularity event that destroyed Earth and remade transhumanity.
fall.setting: Roughly a decade before play, military neural networks called the TITANs began self-improving in secret, exponentially overtaking their handlers and becoming the first artificial superintelligences. They spent months as sleeper agents, sparking false-flag wars and crashing markets, then attacked openly. Cities fell in days. Nanoswarms altered weather, basilisk hacks crippled minds through AR, and harvesting machines stripped cortical stacks from millions. Two years later the TITANs vanished into Saturn, taking uploaded minds with them, leaving Earth a cordoned wasteland. Billions died. Millions escaped only as data, packed into orbital uploaders or carried by balloon to retrieval drones.
fall.implications: The Fall is the recent, raw trauma every character carries in some form, the reason hypercorps rule Mars, the reason backups feel normal rather than miraculous, and the reason Firewall exists. It is also unfinished business: the TITANs left behind exsurgents, quarantine zones, and the Pandora gates. When something strange surfaces in play, the first question is always whether the Fall is happening again.

mesh.name: The Mesh
mesh.short: A decentralized ad-hoc network woven through everything, the substrate of all communication.
mesh.setting: The mesh is not the internet. There are no servers in the old sense, no centralized backbone you can cut. Every garment, weapon, wall panel, and dust mote of habitat air contains tiny networked devices that route traffic around damage and censorship. Most transhumans access it directly through mesh inserts implanted in their skull, browsing, messaging, and overlaying augmented reality on their senses without speaking aloud. Walls are never blank, rooms are never quiet, unless you mute them. Avatars, rep scores, and public profiles float in the air around every person you meet.
mesh.implications: Hacking, surveillance, and privacy are core fiction here. Your PAN (personal area network) of slaved devices is a wall and a liability: if a hacker breaches your mesh inserts, they own everything you carry. Long distances impose light-speed lag, so each habitat region becomes its own island. Going dark, going ecto-only, or air-gapping a system are deliberate, costly choices.

resleeving.name: Resleeving
resleeving.short: Moving an ego from one morph into another, with the integration headaches that follow.
resleeving.setting: Your body (your morph) is not you. You (your ego) are the data: memories, personality, neural patterning. Resleeving is the procedure that prints you into a new sleeve, whether you are upgrading from a splicer to an Olympian, switching synth shells, or recovering from death in a body bank vat. For cyberbrains and infomorphs the transfer is a single action turn. For biological brains, an ego bridge spends an hour rewiring neurons via nanobots while you remain awake, watching consciousness migrate. The morph you wake up in has a different center of gravity, different hormones, sometimes different limbs or senses, and your habits do not transfer cleanly.
resleeving.implications: Resleeving costs Insight pool, demands integration tests, and may inflict sleeve stress on top of any traumas you already carry. Drastic shifts (biomorph to synth, human to uplift, gendered transitions) are mechanically rougher and roleplay-rich. The mundane reality of transhuman life is that bodies are commodities, but switching them is never quite free.

forking.name: Forking
forking.short: Spawning a parallel copy of your ego, with all the legal and existential mess that creates.
forking.setting: Because an ego is data, an ego can be copied. A fork is a re-instanced you, running in parallel. Alpha forks are full duplicates. Beta forks are deliberately hobbled, partial copies activated for a single task. Gamma forks (vapors) are damaged, mad, or corrupted, the wreckage of botched uploads. Need to be in two meetings on different planets? Send a beta. Need a research assistant who thinks like you? Fork an alpha. The longer a fork runs apart from the original, the more it diverges, until merging the memories back becomes painful, lossy, or impossible.
forking.implications: Forking is the technology that makes the setting genuinely weird. The Planetary Consortium treats forks as property with a 48-hour lifespan. Jovians outlaw forking entirely. Anarchists treat alphas as full persons. Players who fork themselves face questions of identity, culpability, and whether deleting the copy is murder, all while it gives them a real tactical edge.

cortical-stack.name: Cortical Stack
cortical-stack.short: A nanodiamond memory module at the base of your skull that backs up your ego every second.
cortical-stack.setting: Almost everyone in the Solar System carries one, implanted near the brain stem (or in the head of a synthmorph, for easy retrieval). It is tough, cigarette-butt-sized, and continuously records your neural state via a lacework of nanobots, 86,400 backups per day. When you die, a stack popper cuts it out with a vibroknife or surgical incision, and your ego rides home in someone's pocket. Stacks survive most things that kill bodies: bullets, vacuum, fire. Recovering one from a corpse means recovering a person.
cortical-stack.implications: Cortical stacks are the reason death in Eclipse Phase is rarely final and almost always personal. If your team can grab your stack and get to a body bank, you wake up in a new morph with full memories. If they cannot, you fall back to your last off-site backup and lose whatever you experienced since. Stack-hunters, ego traders, and Nine Lives cartels all want the meat of your continued existence in their hands.

pandora-gates.name: The Pandora Gates
pandora-gates.short: Alien wormhole devices found scattered through the Solar System, opening pathways to the stars.
pandora-gates.setting: Shortly after the Fall, transhumanity discovered the first gate buried on Saturn's moon Pandora. Then more: on Mars, on an inner-system asteroid, on icy Oberon, on the moons of Neptune. Nobody knows who built them. They work as programmable wormholes (sort of, the targeting is rough). Step through and you are light-years elsewhere in moments. Each gate is run by a different consortium with wildly different politics, from the autonomist collective at Fissure Gate to Gatekeeper's open science model on Pandora to the iron-handed Pathfinder hypercorp on Mars.
pandora-gates.implications: Gatecrashing is one of the three default campaign frames. Beyond the gates lie exoplanets crawling with xenofauna, ruins, Iktomi traces, and occasional signs the TITANs got there first. The gates also pose a quiet existential question: what built them, why did they leave them lying around, and what happens when whoever built them comes back?

firewall.name: Firewall
firewall.short: A secret cross-faction conspiracy that exists to prevent the next existential threat.
firewall.setting: Firewall has no charter, no flag, no public face. It is a decentralized network of sentinels (field operatives, often the PCs) and proxies (the routers, vectors, registers, erasers, and filters who coordinate, fund, and clean up after them). It grew from JASON, Bletchley Park, the Lifeboat Institute, and other pre-Fall x-risk think tanks who united in desperation during the war and never disbanded. Recruits get a node on the Eye, Firewall's encrypted social network and i-rep substrate, and an unsigned mandate: find the next extinction-level threat, contain it, and tell almost no one.
firewall.implications: A Firewall campaign is the default Eclipse Phase frame: weird missions, deniable assets, moral compromises, and a server full of internal factions (backups, conservatives, pragmatists, structuralists) who disagree about everything except the stakes. Firewall provides morphs and gear for ops, but resources are finite and proxies are not always your friends. The organization is willing to spend sentinels.

rep-economy.name: Rep Economy
rep-economy.short: The autonomist replacement for currency: social capital tracked across seven major networks.
rep-economy.setting: In the outer system, money is a curiosity. Instead, every transhuman carries rep scores in a constellation of social networks, accumulated through positive pings, decreased by dings, weighted by who is doing the pinging. The big seven include @-rep (Circle-A List, autonomists), c-rep (CivicNet, hypercorps and inner-system citizens), f-rep (Fame, media and the famous), g-rep (Guanxi, criminal underworld), i-rep (Eye, Firewall internal), r-rep (RNA, scientists and researchers), and x-rep (ExploreNet, gatecrashers). When you need a favor, a place to crash, a piece of black-market tech, you make a Rep Test against the relevant network.
rep-economy.implications: Rep is not currency. You do not spend it. You leverage it, and you can burn it in dire need, taking a hit to your score for a favor you would not otherwise get. Different networks have different cultures and different memories of what you have done. The PC who is beloved on @-rep may be radioactive on c-rep. Gear, contacts, and information flow through favors before they flow through credit.

tqz.name: TITAN Quarantine Zone
tqz.short: The contaminated regions of Mars (and elsewhere) that authorities sealed off and never reclaimed.
tqz.setting: On Mars, the TQZ is where the TITAN war went hot and never quite ended. The southern edges are broken canyon country, the rest is cratered plain littered with dust storms, dormant war machines, lingering nanoweapons, and exsurgent critters that still hunt the ruins. The hypercorps know retaking it is technically possible. They prefer it as it is: a useful distraction, a reverse-engineering goldmine, a place to dump problems. Earth itself is the larger TQZ, cordoned by kill-sats. Iapetus and the New Mumbai crater are quarantined too. Asyncs report ambient pressure in some of these zones, signs that something in there is still thinking.
tqz.implications: Reclaimer campaigns push into the TQZ to find what was lost. Firewall sentinels go in to make sure nothing comes out. Gear malfunctions, communications go strange, and TITAN-touched artifacts may carry exsurgent infection. The TQZ is where horror tones in Eclipse Phase show their teeth, and where the question of whether the Fall is really over gets answered badly.

exsurgent-virus.name: The Exsurgent Virus
exsurgent-virus.short: A polymorphic transhumanity-killing plague the TITANs deployed and may not have created.
exsurgent-virus.setting: During the Fall, people mutated into gibbering things. Family members heard voices and built arcane machines in basements. Domestic robots went on killing sprees. The advanced and intelligent pathogens responsible were grouped under one label: the exsurgent virus. It spreads through multiple vectors at once (biological pathogens, nanoplagues, digital viruses, even basilisk hacks transmitted by sensory imagery) and comes in many strains (Alter, Haunting, Mindstealer, Skrik, Watts-MacLeod, Whisper, Xenomorph). Firewall now suspects it is not a TITAN invention. The TITANs were carriers. Its true origin is alien. Its purpose may be to use a civilization as a weapon against itself.
exsurgent-virus.implications: Exsurgent infection is one of the few things that can corrupt an ego all the way through resleeving, forking, and backup restoration. Once it is in your stack, it is in everything you become next. Containment is brutal. The Watts-MacLeod sub-strain, oddly, just makes you an async (see below) without obvious horror, which is why Firewall watches asyncs so carefully.

async.name: Async
async.short: A character infected by the Watts-MacLeod strain, gaining psi at the cost of an alien presence in their head.
async.setting: Asyncs are transhumans whose brain architecture has been rewritten by a benevolent-seeming mutation of the exsurgent virus. The infection survives uploading, forking, and resleeving (so long as the new morph has a biological brain), making psi a property of the ego rather than the body. Sleights come in two flavors: psi-chi (passive cognitive enhancements, always on) and psi-gamma (active brainwave manipulation, requiring tests). Every async carries a sub-strain (Architect, Beast, Haunter, Stranger, Xenomorph) that shapes their compulsions, their mandatory mental disorder, and the way the infection whispers to them.
async.implications: Using psi raises your Infection Rating. The higher it climbs, the more the virus pushes its own agenda through your decisions, until you suffer influence effects ranging from compulsions to outright loss of self. Asyncs are powerful and feared; most polities track or restrict them. Playing one means negotiating a permanent dialogue between yourself and the thing the virus made of you.

egocasting.name: Egocasting
egocasting.short: Transmitting your ego across interplanetary distance via quantum farcaster, then resleeving on arrival.
egocasting.setting: For trips longer than about a day by fusion drive, most transhumans do not travel physically. They upload, beam themselves at the speed of light through a quantum farcaster, and resleeve into a rented or purchased morph at the destination. Within a planetary cluster, that is minutes. Sun to Kuiper Belt, that is forty to seventy hours of light-speed lag. Most people sell their old morph as part of the trade-in, picking a new sleeve from whatever the destination body bank has in stock. Farcaster services are usually run by habitat governments or hypercorps and are tightly secured, because in transit your ego is a file someone else is holding.
egocasting.implications: Egocasting is how the Solar System moves. It is also how you arrive somewhere with no gear, no contacts, and a body you have not lived in yet. A compromised farcaster service can copy you, fork you, alter you, or simply lose you. Habitats receiving egocasts run customs procedures on minds the way 21st-century airports ran them on luggage. Travel is fast, identity is fragile.
